name: Finding fossil man
trans: 寻找“化石人类”

name: Why are legends handed down by storytellers useful?
trans: 为什么由讲故事的人传承下来的传说具有价值（或者说：为什么这些传说是有用的呢？）

name: We can read of things that happened 5, 000 years ago in the Near East,
trans: 我们可以了解到发生在5000年前近东地区的事情。

name: where people first learned to write.
trans: 人们最初学习书写的地方。

name: But there are some parts of the world where even now people cannot write.
trans: 但是，在世界上的一些地方，直到现在人们仍然无法写字。

name: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
trans: 他们唯一能够保存自己历史的方式，就是将这些故事作为传奇或神话传说，一代又一代地由讲故事的人传承下去。

name: These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago,
trans: 这些传说很有价值，因为它们能为我们提供关于很久以前人们迁徙情况的线索。

name: but none could write down what they did.
trans: 但是没有人能够写下他们到底做了什么。

name: Anthropologists wondered where the remote ancestors of the Polynesian peoples now living in the Pacific Islandscame from.
trans: 人类学家一直想知道，如今居住在太平洋岛屿上的波利尼西亚人的远古祖先究竟来自何处。

name: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2, 000 years ago.
trans: 关于这些人的传说表明，其中一些人大约在2000年前从印度尼西亚移民过来的。

name: But the first people who were like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten.
trans: 但是，那些与我们相似的最早的人类生活在太久以前了，以至于他们的传说（如果有的话）早已被人们遗忘了。

name: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first 'modern men' came from.
trans: 因此，考古学家既没有历史记录，也没有传说可以帮助他们查明最早的“现代人类”来自何处。

name: Fortunately, however, ancient men made tools of stone, especially flint,
trans: 然而，幸运的是，古代人类使用了石头（尤其是燧石）来制作工具。

name: because this is easier to shape than other kinds.
trans: 因为这种材料比其他类型的材料更容易加工（或塑形）。

name: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
trans: 他们可能还使用过木材和兽皮，但这些材料都已经腐烂掉了。

name: Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
trans: 石头是不会腐烂的，因此那些远古时代的工具至今仍然保存完好；而那些制造这些工具的人的骨头早已消失得无影无踪了。

name: How much of each year do spiders spend killing insects?
trans: 蜘蛛每年有多少时间用于捕杀昆虫？

name: Why, you may wonder, should spiders be our friends?
trans: 你可能会想：为什么蜘蛛应该成为我们的朋友呢？

name: Because they destroy so many insects, and insects include some of the greatest enemies of the human race.
trans: 因为它们会消灭大量的昆虫，而昆虫中有一些是人类最大的天敌。

name: Insects would make it impossible for us to live in the world;
trans: 如果昆虫存在的话，我们将无法在这个世界上生存。

name: they would devour all our crops and kill our flocks and herds,
trans: 它们会吃光我们所有的庄稼，杀死我们的牲畜（包括羊群和牛群）。

name: if it were not for the protection we get from insect eating animals.
trans: 如果不是因为那些以昆虫为食的动物所提供的保护，情况就会大不相同了。

name: We owe a lot to the birds and beasts who eat insects
trans: 我们非常感谢那些以昆虫为食的鸟类和动物。

name: but all of them put together kill only a fraction of the number destroyed by spiders.
trans: 但即便把它们全部加在一起，它们所造成的破坏量也只相当于蜘蛛所造成的破坏量的很小一部分。

name: Moreover, unlike some of the other insect eaters, spiders never do the least harm to us or our belongings.
trans: 此外，与其他一些以昆虫为食的动物不同，蜘蛛从未对我们或我们的财物造成过任何伤害。

name: Spiders are not insects, as many people think, nor even nearly related to them.
trans: 蜘蛛并不是昆虫，尽管许多人认为它们属于昆虫；实际上，它们与昆虫之间几乎没有亲缘关系。

name: One can tell the difference almost at a glance, for a spider always has eight legs and an insect never more than six.
trans: 几乎一眼就能看出区别：蜘蛛总是有八条腿，而昆虫的腿数量从来不会超过六条。

name: How many spiders are engaged in this work on our behalf?
trans: 有多少只蜘蛛在为我们完成这项工作呢？

name: One authority on spiders made a census of the spiders in a grass field in the south of England,
trans: 一位研究蜘蛛的专家对英格兰南部一片草地上的蜘蛛进行了统计调查。

name: and he estimated that there were more than 2, 250, 000 in one acre;
trans: 他估计每英亩的面积上大约有超过225万（个）这样的单位。

name: that is something like 6, 000, 000 spiders of different kinds on a football pitch.
trans: 那相当于在足球场上放了大约600万只各种各样的蜘蛛。

name: Spiders are busy for at least half the year in killing insects.
trans: 蜘蛛至少有一半年的时间都在捕杀昆虫。

name: It is impossible to make more than the wildest guess at how many they kill, but they are hungry creatures, not content with only three meals a day.
trans: 我们根本无法准确猜测它们到底杀死了多少动物；它们是饥饿的生物，一天三顿饭显然远远无法满足它们的需求。

name: It has been estimated that the weight of all the insects destroyed by spiders in Britain in one year would be greater than the total weight of all the human beings in the country.
trans: 据估计，英国的蜘蛛在一年内消灭的所有昆虫的重量，将超过该国所有人类的总重量。

name: Matterhorn man
trans: “马特洪峰人”（Matterhorn man）是指那些曾在马特洪峰（Matterhorn）进行登山活动的人。这个称呼可能源于历史上一些著名的登山者，或者是对那些勇敢挑战这座阿尔卑斯山高峰的人的统称。

name: What was the main objective of early mountain climbers?
trans: 早期登山者的主要目标是什么？

name: Modern alpinists try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport,
trans: 现代登山者会选择那些能够带来最佳攀登体验的路线来攀登山脉。

name: and the more difficult it is, the more highly it is regarded.
trans: 难度越大，其价值或地位也就越高。

name: In the pioneering days however, this was not the case at all.
trans: 然而，在创业初期，情况完全不是这样的。

name: The early climbers were looking for the easiest way to the top because the summit was the prize they sought,
trans: 早期的登山者们都在寻找通往山顶的最简单路径，因为山顶就是他们追求的目标。

name: especially if it had never been attained before.
trans: 尤其是当这个目标以前从未被实现过的时候。

name: It is true that during their explorations they often faced difficulties and dangers of the most perilous nature,
trans: 的确，在他们的探索过程中，他们经常面临极其危险和充满挑战的处境。

name: equipped in a manner which would make a modern climber shudder at the thought,
trans: 这些装备的配置程度之高，足以让现代登山者听到后不寒而栗。

name: but they did not go out of their way to court such excitement.
trans: 但他们并没有刻意去营造这种热闹的氛围（或：他们并没有主动去引发人们的兴奋情绪）。

name: They had a single aim, a solitary goal -- the top!
trans: 他们只有一个目标，一个唯一的目的——那就是登上巅峰！

name: It is hard for us to realize nowadays how difficult it was for the pioneers.
trans: 如今，我们很难想象那些开拓者当时所面临的困难有多大。

name: Except for one or two places such as Zermatt and Chamonix, which had rapidly become popular.
trans: 除了泽马特（Zermatt）和夏蒙尼（Chamonix）这样迅速走红的地方之外，其他地区的情况都差不多。

name: Alpine villages tended to be impoverished settlements cut off from civilization by the high mountains.
trans: 阿尔卑斯山区的村庄往往都是贫困的聚居地，被高大的山脉与外界隔离开来。

name: Such inns as there were were generally dirty and flea-ridden;
trans: 那些当时的客栈通常都很脏，而且到处都是跳蚤。

name: the food simply local cheese accompanied by bread often twelve months old,
trans: 这些食物只是普通的本地奶酪，配着面包；而那些面包往往已经存放了十二个月之久。

name: all washed down with coarse wine.
trans: （所有东西都被粗糙的葡萄酒冲走了。）

name: Often a valley boasted no inn at all, and climbers found shelter wherever they could --
trans: 很多时候，山谷里根本没有客栈可供休息；登山者们只能随便找个地方暂避风雪或等待救援。

name: sometimes with the local priest (who was usually as poor as his parishioners),
trans: 有时候会和当地的牧师一起（这位牧师通常和他的教区居民一样贫穷）。

name: sometimes with shepherds or cheese-makers.
trans: 有时候，这些活动会与牧羊人或奶酪制造商们一起进行。

name: Invariably the background was the same:dirt and poverty, and very uncomfortable.
trans: 背景总是相同的：肮脏、贫穷，而且环境极其恶劣（让人感到非常不适）。

name: For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets at home,
trans: 对于那些习惯了在家享用七道菜的晚餐、并睡在柔软的亚麻床单上的男人来说，

name: the change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.
trans: 对阿尔卑斯山脉来说，这种变化肯定非常巨大、非常艰难（或者说：这种变化对阿尔卑斯山脉的环境或生态系统造成了极大的影响）。

name: Seeing hands
trans: “看见手”（Seeing Hands）

name: How did Vera disover she had this gift of second sight?
trans: 维拉是如何发现自己拥有这种“预知能力”的呢？

name: Several cases have been reported in Russia recently of people who can read and detect colours with their fingers, and even see through solid doors and walls.
trans: 最近在俄罗斯报告了几起这样的案例：有些人能够用手指识别颜色、感知物体的颜色；甚至能够“看穿”坚固的门和墙壁。

name: One case concerns an 11-year-old schoolgirl Vera Petrova,
trans: 其中一个案例涉及一名11岁的女学生维拉·彼得罗娃。

name: who has normal vision but who can also perceive things with different parts of her skin, and through solid walls.
trans: 这个人拥有正常的视力，但也能通过皮肤的不同部位，甚至穿过坚固的墙壁来感知事物。

name: This ability was first noticed by her father.
trans: 这种能力最初是由她的父亲注意到的。

name: One day she came into his office and happened to put her hands on the door of a locked safe.
trans: 有一天，她走进他的办公室，不小心碰到了一个上锁的保险箱的门。

name: Suddenly she asked her father why he kept so many old newspapers locked away there,
trans: 突然，她问她的父亲：为什么要把这么多旧报纸锁在那个地方呢？

name: and even described the way they were done up in bundles.
trans: 甚至还描述了它们是如何被打包成束的。

name: Vera's curious talent was brought to the notice of a scientific research institute in the town of Ulyanovsk, near where she lives,
trans: 维拉的这种好奇心与探索精神被她居住地附近的乌里扬诺夫斯克市的一家科学研究机构注意到了。

name: and in April she was given a series of tests by a special commission of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federal Republic.
trans: 四月份，她接受了一系列由俄罗斯联邦卫生部特别委员会组织的检查。

name: During these tests she was able to read a newspaper through an opaque screen and, stranger still,
trans: 在这些测试中，她能够透过一块不透明的屏幕阅读报纸；更奇怪的是……

name: by moving her elbow over a child's game of Lotto she was able to describe the figures and colours printed on it;
trans: 她将肘部放在一个儿童玩的“Lotto”游戏卡片上，从而能够描述卡片上印有的图案和颜色。

name: and, in another instance, wearing stockings and slippers,
trans: 还有另一个例子：她穿着长袜和拖鞋。

name: to make out with her foot the outlines and colours of a picture hidden under a carpet.
trans: 用她的脚去感受、辨认出隐藏在地毯下的那幅画的轮廓和颜色。

name: Other experiments showed that her knees and shoulders had a similar sensitivity.
trans: 其他实验表明，她的膝盖和肩膀的敏感度也相似。

name: During all these tests Vera was blindfold; and indeed, except when blindfold she lacked the ability to perceive things with her skin.
trans: 在所有这些测试中，维拉都被蒙住了眼睛；事实上，除非她的眼睛没有被蒙住，否则她就无法通过皮肤来感知周围的事物了。

name: It was also found that although she could perceive things with her fingers this ability ceased the moment her hands were wet.
trans: 还发现，尽管她可以用手指感知物体，但一旦她的手变湿，这种能力就会立刻消失。

name: Youth
trans: 青年；年轻人

name: How does the writer like to treat young people?
trans: 这位作家是如何描写年轻人的呢？

name: People are always talking about 'the problem of youth'.
trans: 人们总是谈论“年轻人的问题”。

name: If there is one -- which I take leave to doubt
trans: 如果真有这样的东西的话（不过我对此表示怀疑）……

name: -- then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
trans: 那么，创造这种东西的其实是老年人，而不是年轻人自己。

name: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings
trans: 让我们回归到基本事实：年轻人终究也是人。

name: -- people just like their elders.
trans: 人们总是喜欢和自己的长辈一样。

name: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one:
trans: 老人和年轻人之间只有一个区别：

name: the young man has a glorious future before him
trans: 这个年轻人前途光明，充满希望。

name: and the old one has a splendid future behind him: and maybe that is where the rub is.
trans: 而那个旧的东西已经拥有了一个辉煌的未来；也许问题就出在这里。

name: When I was a teenager, I felt that I was just young and uncertain --
trans: 当我还是个青少年的时候，我觉得自己只是个年轻且缺乏自信的人罢了。

name: that I was a new boy in a huge school,
trans: 我当时只是那所大型学校里的一名新生罢了。

name: and I would have been very pleased to be regarded as something so interesting as a problem.
trans: 如果我能被看作是一个“有趣的问题”（即一个值得研究或关注的问题），我会非常高兴的。

name: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity,
trans: 首先，成为一个“问题”（即被视作需要解决的问题）会让你获得某种特定的“身份”或地位。

name: and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
trans: 而这正是年轻人正在积极寻求的东西之一。

name: I find young people exciting.
trans: 我觉得年轻人非常令人兴奋。

name: They have an air of freedom,
trans: 他们身上散发着一种自由的气息。

name: and they have not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
trans: 他们既没有对崇高理想的执着追求，也没有对舒适生活的热爱。

name: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
trans: 他们不是那种急于向上爬、渴望在社会中取得成功的人；同时，他们对物质财富也没有丝毫的执着或渴望。

name: All this seems to me to link them with life and the origins of things.
trans: 在我看来，所有这些都将它们与生命以及万物的起源联系在了一起。

name: It's as if they were in some sense cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
trans: 他们仿佛是某种宇宙中的存在，与我们这些生活在郊区的生物形成了鲜明而矛盾的对比——既充满暴力，又充满美感。

name: All that is in my mind when I meet a young person.
trans: 每当我遇到一个年轻人时，我脑海中想到的就是这些。

name: He may be conceited, ill-mannered,  presumptuous or fatuous,  but I do not turn for protection to dreary cliches about respect for elders --
trans: 他或许自负、举止粗鲁、傲慢无礼，或者愚蠢至极；但我绝不会求助于那些陈腐的、关于“尊敬长辈”的空洞口号来寻求保护。

name: as if mere age were a reason for respect.
trans: 仿佛年龄本身就能成为值得尊重的理由似的……

name: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
trans: 我承认我们彼此平等；如果我认为他错了，我会以平等的身份与他争论。

name: The sporting spirit
trans: 体育精神

name: How does the writer describe sport at the international level?
trans: 作者是如何描述国际层面的体育运动的？

name: I am always amazed when I hear people saying that sport creates goodwill between the nations, and that if only the common peoples of the world could meet one another at football or cricket, they would have no inclination to meet on the battlefield.
trans: 每当听到有人说体育能够促进国家之间的友好关系，并认为如果全世界的人们都能在足球或板球比赛中相聚，他们就不会有在战场上交锋的冲动时，我总是感到非常惊讶。

name: Even if one didn't know from concrete examples (the 1936 Olympic Games, for instance) that international sporting contests lead to orgies of hatred, one could deduce it from general principles.
trans: 即使没有具体的例子（比如1936年的奥运会）来证明国际体育赛事会引发激烈的仇恨情绪，人们也可以根据一些基本原理推断出这一点。

name: Nearly all the sports practised nowadays are competitive.
trans: 如今，几乎所有的体育运动都具有竞争性。

name: You play to win, and the game has little meaning unless you do your utmost to win.
trans: 你玩游戏是为了赢；只有当你竭尽全力去争取胜利时，这个游戏才真正有意义。

name: On the village green, where you pick up sides and no feeling of local patriotism is involved, it is possible to play simply for the fun and exercise: but as soon as a the question of prestige arises, as soon as you feel that you and some larger unit will be disgraced if you lose, the most savage combative instincts are aroused.
trans: 在村里的空地上，大家只是为了娱乐和锻炼而参与比赛，此时并不会产生任何地方主义情绪；但一旦涉及到荣誉和面子的问题，一旦你意识到如果输了，自己或所在的团队会蒙羞，最激烈的战斗欲望就会被激发出来。

name: Anyone who has played even in a school football match knows this.
trans: 任何参加过学校足球比赛的人都知道这一点。

name: At the international level, sport is frankly mimic warfare.
trans: 在国际层面上，体育运动实际上在模仿战争。

name: But the significant thing is not the behaviour of the players but the attitude of the spectators:
trans: 但真正重要的是观众的态度，而不是玩家的行为。

name: and, behind the spectators, of the nations who work themselves into furies over these absurd contests,
trans: 而在观众们的身后，还有那些为这些荒谬的比赛而疯狂投入、全力以赴的各国人民……

name: and seriously believe -- at any rate for short periods -- that running, jumping and kicking a ball are tests of national virtue.
trans: 并且我真的相信——至少在短时间内是这样——跑步、跳跃和踢球是检验一个国家人民品德的方式。

name: Bats
trans: 蝙蝠

name: In what way does echo-location in bats play an utilitarian role?
trans: 蝙蝠的回声定位功能在哪些方面发挥了实际作用（即具有实用价值）？

name: Not all sounds made by animals serve as language, and we have only to turn to that extraordinary discovery of echo-location in bats to see a case in which the voice plays a strictly utilitarian role.
trans: 并非所有动物发出的声音都属于“语言”范畴；我们只需看看蝙蝠的回声定位能力这一非凡的生理现象，就能明白：在某些情况下，声音仅仅起着实用性的作用（即用于获取信息或导航）。

name: To get a full appreciation of what this means we must turn first to some recent human inventions.
trans: 要充分理解这意味着什么，我们首先必须看看一些最近的人类发明。

name: Everyone knows that if he shouts in the vicinity of a wall or a mountainside, an echo will come back.
trans: 大家都知道，如果在墙壁或山坡附近大声喊叫，就会听到回声。

name: The further off this solid obstruction, the longer time will elapse for the return of the echo.
trans: 距离这个固体障碍物越远，回声返回所需的时间就越长。

name: A sound made by tapping on the hull of a ship will be reflected from the sea bottom, and by measuring the time interval between the taps and the receipt of the echoes the depth of the sea at that point can be calculated.
trans: 当敲击船体时，声音会从海底反射回来；通过测量敲击声与接收到回声之间的时间间隔，就可以计算出该位置的海水深度。

name: So was born the echo-sounding apparatus, now in general use in ships.
trans: 就这样，这种能够反射声波的装置应运而生，并且如今已被广泛应用于各种船舶中。

name: Every solid object will reflect a sound, varying according to the size and nature of the object.
trans: 每个固体物体都会反射声音，反射效果会因物体的大小和材质而有所不同。

name: A shoal of fish will do this.
trans: 一群鱼也会这样做。

name: So it is a comparatively simple step from locating the sea bottom to locating a shoal of fish.
trans: 因此，从确定海底的位置到找到鱼群的位置，这个过程相对来说是相当简单的。

name: With experience, and with improved apparatus, it is now possible not only to locate a shoal but to tell if it is herring, cod, or other well-known fish, by the pattern of its echo.
trans: 凭借丰富的经验以及更先进的设备，现在不仅能够定位鱼群的位置，还能通过鱼群产生的回声信号来判断它们是鲱鱼、鳕鱼，还是其他常见的鱼类。

name: It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes,
trans: 研究发现，某些蝙蝠会发出鸣叫声；通过接收这些鸣叫声的回声，

name: they can locate and steer clear of obstacles -- or locate flying insects on which they feed.
trans: 它们能够识别并避开障碍物，同时也能找到可供它们捕食的飞虫。

name: This echo-location in bats is often compared with radar, the principle of which is similar.
trans: 蝙蝠的回声定位系统常被比作雷达，因为它们的工作原理是相似的。

name: Trading standards
trans: 交易标准

name: What makes trading between rich countries difficult?
trans: 是什么让富裕国家之间的贸易变得如此困难呢？

name: Chickens slaughtered in the United States, claim officials in Brussels, are not fit to grace European tables.
trans: 布鲁塞尔的官员声称，在美国被屠宰的鸡肉不符合进入欧洲市场的标准，因此不适合出现在欧洲人的餐桌上。

name: No, say the Americans: our fowl are fine, we simply clean them in a different way.
trans: 不，美国人会这么说：“我们的家禽没什么问题，只是我们清洗它们的方式有所不同罢了。”

name: These days, it is differences in national regulations, far more than tariffs, that put sand in the wheels of trade between rich countries.
trans: 如今，阻碍富裕国家之间贸易发展的因素主要是各国法规之间的差异，而非关税本身。

name: It is not just farmers who are complaining.
trans: 不仅仅是农民在抱怨。

name: An electric razor that meets the European Union's safety standards must be approved by American testers before it can be sold in the United States, and an American-made dialysis machine needs the EU's okay before it hits the market in Europe.
trans: 任何符合欧盟安全标准的电动剃须刀，在美国销售之前都必须经过美国相关机构的检测和批准；同样，任何在美国制造的透析设备，在欧洲市场上销售之前也必须获得欧盟的认可。

name: As it happens, a razor that is safe in Europe is unlikely to electrocute Americans.
trans: 事实上，那种在欧洲使用起来安全的剃须刀，不太可能对美国人造成触电危险。

name: So, ask businesses on both sides of the Atlantic, why have two lots of tests where one would do?
trans: 那么，不妨问问大西洋两岸的企业：为什么明明只需要进行一次测试，却非要重复进行两次呢？

name: Politicians agree, in principle, so America and the EU have been trying to reach a deal which would eliminate the need to double-test many products.
trans: 从原则上讲，各国政界人士都持一致意见；因此，美国和欧盟一直在努力达成一项协议，以消除对许多产品进行重复检测的必要性。

name: They hope to finish in time for a trade summit between America and the EU on May 28th.
trans: 他们希望能在5月28日美国与欧盟之间的贸易峰会之前完成所有工作。

name: Although negotiators are optimistic, the details are complex enough that they may be hard-pressed to get a deal at all.
trans: 尽管谈判代表们持乐观态度，但相关细节过于复杂，他们可能很难达成任何协议。

name: Why? One difficulty is to construct the agreements.
trans: 为什么呢？其中一个难点在于如何制定这些协议（即如何确保各方能够就相关条款达成一致）。

name: The Americans would happily reach one accord on standards for medical devices and then hammer out different pacts covering, say, electronic goods and drug manufacturing.
trans: 美国人很乐意就医疗器械的标准达成一致，随后再分别就电子产品和药品制造等领域制定具体的协议。

name: The EU -- following fine continental traditions -- wants agreement on general principles,
trans: 欧盟遵循欧洲大陆的传统，希望各方能够就一些基本原则达成共识。

name: which could be applied to many types of products and perhaps extended to other countries.
trans: 这种方法可以应用于许多类型的产品，并且有可能推广到其他国家。

name: Royal espionage
trans: 皇家间谍活动

name: What important thing did King Alfred learn when he penetrated the Danish camp of Guthrum?
trans: 当阿尔弗雷德国王突袭古思伦的丹麦营地时，他学到了什么重要的东西？

name: Alfred the Great acted as his own spy, visiting Danish camps disguised as a minstrel.
trans: 阿尔弗雷德大帝亲自担任间谍，他伪装成吟游诗人，潜入丹麦的营地进行侦察。

name: In those days wandering minstrels were welcome everywhere.
trans: 在那些日子里，流浪的吟游诗人随处都受到欢迎。

name: They were not fighting men, and their harp was their passport.
trans: 他们并非战士，他们的竖琴便是他们的“通行证”——一种象征身份或文化的标志。

name: Alfred had learned many of their ballads in his youth and could vary his programme with acrobatic tricks and simple conjuring.
trans: 阿尔弗雷德在年轻时就学会了他们许多民谣歌曲；他还可以通过表演杂技技巧和简单的魔术来丰富自己的表演节目。

name: While Alfred's little army slowly began to gather at Athelney, the king himself set out to penetrate the camp of Guthrum, the commander of the Danish invaders.
trans: 当阿尔弗雷德的小军队开始在阿瑟尔尼（Athelney）集结时，国王本人则亲自率领部队前往丹麦入侵者的营地——那里由古思伦（Guthrum）指挥。

name: These had settled down for the winter at Chippenham: thither Alfred went.
trans: 这些动物已经在奇彭纳姆过冬了；阿尔弗雷德也前往了那里。

name: He noticed at once that discipline was slack: the Danes had the self-confidence of conquerors, and their security precautions were casual.
trans: 他立刻察觉到纪律松弛的情况：丹麦人拥有征服者的自信，他们的安全防范措施也非常松懈。

name: They lived well, on the proceeds of raids on neighbouring regions.
trans: 他们靠着对邻近地区的劫掠所得，过上了富足的生活。

name: There they collected women as well as food and drink, and a life of ease had made them soft.
trans: 他们在那里收集了妇女、食物和饮料；安逸的生活使他们变得软弱、缺乏斗志。

name: Alfred stayed in the camp a week before he returned to Athelney.
trans: 阿尔弗雷德在营地待了一周后，才返回阿瑟尔尼。

name: The force there assembled was trivial compared with the Danish horde.
trans: 那里集结的兵力与丹麦大军相比微不足道。

name: But Alfred had deduced that the Danes were no longer fit for prolonged battle: and that their commissariat had no organization, but depended on irregular raids.
trans: 但他察觉到：丹麦军队已不再适合进行长时间的战斗；他们的后勤补给体系毫无组织可言，只能依靠零星的袭击来维持。

name: So, faced with the Danish advance, Alfred did not risk open battle but harried the enemy.
trans: 因此，在面对丹麦军队的进攻时，阿尔弗雷德没有选择正面交锋，而是不断骚扰敌人。

name: He was constantly on the move, drawing the Danes after him.
trans: 他始终处于移动状态，引诱丹麦军队跟随自己行动。

name: His patrols halted the raiding parties: hunger assailed the Danish army.
trans: 他的巡逻队成功阻止了那些袭击行动；丹麦军队逐渐陷入了饥饿的困境。

name: Now Alfred began a long series of skirmishes -- and within a month the Danes had surrendered.
trans: 随后，阿尔弗雷德展开了一系列小规模战斗——一个月内，丹麦军队便投降了。

name: The episode could reasonably serve as a unique epic of royal espionage!
trans: 这一事件完全可以被视为一部关于王室间谍活动的独特史诗！

name: Silicon valley
trans: 硅谷

name: What does the computer industry thrive on apart from anarchy?
trans: 除了混乱（或无序的状态）之外，计算机行业还依靠什么来蓬勃发展呢？

name: Technology trends may push Silicon Valley back to the future.
trans: 科技趋势可能会让硅谷重新回到“过去”的状态（即回到某种传统或早期的发展阶段）。

name: Carver Mead, a pioneer in integrated circuits and a professor of computer science at the California Institute of Technology, notes there are now workstations that enable engineers to design, test and produce chips right on their desks, much the way and editor creates a newsletter on a Macintosh.
trans: 卡弗·米德（Carver Mead）是集成电路领域的先驱，同时也是加州理工学院的计算机科学教授。他指出，如今已经有了这样的工作站：工程师们可以在自己的办公桌上直接设计、测试和制造芯片——就像使用 Macintosh 电脑来编写新闻稿一样简单方便。

name: As the time and cost of making a chip drop to a few days and a few hundred dollars, engineers may soon be free to let their imaginations soar without being penalized by expensive failures.
trans: 随着制造芯片所需的时间和成本降至几天以及几百美元的水平，工程师们很快就可以自由发挥他们的想象力了，而无需再为昂贵的失败成本而担忧。

name: Mead predicts that inventors will be able to perfect powerful customized chips over a weekend at the office --
trans: Mead预测，发明者们将能够在周末的办公室里，通过简单的操作就能完善那些功能强大、且能够根据需求定制的芯片。

name: spawning a new generation of garage start-ups and giving the U. S.  a jump on its foreign rivals in getting new products to market fast.
trans: 这催生了一代新的车库创业公司（即那些在自家车库里创立的小型企业），使美国在将新产品快速推向市场方面领先于其外国竞争对手。

name: 'We've got more garages with smart people,' Mead observes. 'We really thrive on anarchy. '
trans: “我们拥有更多配备了智能设备的车库，以及更多聪明的人，”米德观察到。“我们其实非常喜欢这种无序的状态（即‘混乱’）。”

name: And on Asians. Already, orientals and Asian Americans constitute the majority of the engineering staffs at many Valley firms.
trans: 至于亚洲人：在许多硅谷的科技公司中，东方人以及亚裔美国人已经占据了工程团队的大部分职位。

name: And Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Indian engineers are graduating in droves from California's colleges.
trans: 越来越多的中国、韩国、菲律宾和印度的工程师从加利福尼亚的大学毕业。

name: As the heads of next-generation start-ups, these Asian innovators can draw on customs and languages to forge tighter links with crucial Pacific Rim markets.
trans: 作为下一代初创企业的领导者，这些亚洲创新者可以利用当地的习俗和语言，与太平洋沿岸的重要市场建立更加紧密的联系。

name: For instance, Alex Au, a Stanford Ph. D. from Hong Kong, has set up a Taiwan factory to challenge Japan's near lock on the memory-chip market.
trans: 例如，来自香港的斯坦福大学博士Alex Au在台湾建立了一家工厂，旨在挑战日本对内存芯片市场的近乎垄断地位。

name: India-born N. Damodar Reddy's tiny California company reopened an AT&T chip plant in Kansas City last spring with financing from the state of Missouri.
trans: 出生于印度的N. Damodar Reddy在加利福尼亚创立的小型企业，去年春天在密苏里州的资助下，重新启用了AT&T在堪萨斯城的生产工厂。

name: Before it becomes a retirement village, Silicon Valley may prove a classroom for building a global business.
trans: 在变成一个养老社区之前，硅谷或许会成为培养全球性企业的摇篮。

name: How to grow old
trans: 如何安享晚年

name: What, according to the author, is the best way to overcome the fear of death as you get older?
trans: 根据作者的观点，随着年龄的增长，克服对死亡的恐惧的最佳方法是什么？

name: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.
trans: 有些老年人被对死亡的恐惧所折磨（或：有些老年人深受对死亡的恐惧的困扰）。

name: In the young there is a justification for this feeling.
trans: 在年轻人身上，这种情感是情有可原的。

name: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle
trans: 那些有理由担心自己会在战斗中丧生的年轻人们

name: may justifiably feel bitter in the thought
trans: 有理由感到愤懑（或痛苦）

name: that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
trans: 他们被剥夺了生活中最美好的东西。

name: But in an old man who has known human joys and sorrows,
trans: 但对于一个经历过人生种种喜怒哀乐的老人来说，

name: and has achieved whatever work it was in him to do,
trans: 并且已经完成了他所能完成的所有工作。

name: the fear of death is somewhat abject and ignoble.
trans: 对死亡的恐惧在某种程度上是卑劣且可耻的。

name: The best way to overcome it--so at least it seems to me--
trans: 克服这个问题的最佳方法——至少在我看来是这样……

name: is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal,
trans: 其目的在于逐渐拓宽自己的视野，使自己的兴趣变得更为广泛且不再那么个人化；

name: until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede,
trans: 直到自我的界限一点点消融，

name: and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
trans: 自己的生命逐渐融入到宇宙的生命之中。

name: An individual human existence should be like a river--
trans: 一个人的存在应当像一条河流——

name: small at first, narrowly contained within its banks,
trans: 起初很小，被两岸紧紧束缚；

name: and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls.
trans: 它激情澎湃地冲过巨石、飞跃过瀑布。

name: Gradually the river grows wider, the banks recede, the waters flow more quietly,
trans: 随着时间的推移，河流变得越来越宽广，两岸逐渐后退，水流也变得更加平缓；

name: and in the end, without any visiblebreak, they become merged in the sea,
trans: 最终，它毫无阻碍地融入大海，

name: and painlessly lose their individual being.
trans: 悄无声息地失去了自身的独立性。

name: The man who, in old age can see his life in this way,
trans: 那些在晚年能够以这种方式看待自己人生的人，

name: will not suffer from the fear of death,
trans: 就不会害怕死亡，

name: since the things he cares for will continue.
trans: 因为他们所珍视的一切都会继续存在下去。

name: And if, with the decay of vitality, weariness increases,
trans: 那么，随着生命力的衰退，疲劳感也会随之增加。

name: the thought of rest will be not unwelcome.
trans: 一想到可以休息，我就会感到非常高兴（或：休息的想法让我很受欢迎）。

name: I should wish to die while still at work,
trans: 我真希望自己还能在工作的时候就死去。

name: knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do,
trans: 知道其他人会继续做那些我再也无法完成的事情……

name: and content in the thought that what was possible has been done.
trans: 并且心中想着：那些原本被认为不可能实现的事情，现在已经都实现了。

name: Banks and their customers
trans: 银行及其客户

name: Why is there no risk to the customer when a bank prints the customer's name on his cheques?
trans: 为什么当银行在客户的支票上打印客户的名字时，这对客户来说没有任何风险呢？

name: When anyone opens a current account at a bank, he is lending the bank money,
trans: 当任何人向银行开设一个活期账户时，实际上就是在把钱借给银行。

name: repayment of which he may demand at any time either in cash or by drawing a cheque in favour of another person.
trans: 他可以随时要求偿还这笔款项，既可以要求以现金形式支付，也可以要求开一张支票转给另一个人。

name: Primarily, the banker-customer relationship is that of debtor and creditor--
trans: 从根本上说，银行与客户之间的关系就是债务人与债权人的关系。

name: who is which depending on whether the customer's account is in credit or is overdrawn.
trans: 具体是哪位客户，取决于该客户的账户是处于贷方状态（即有余额）还是处于透支状态（即余额为负）。

name: But, in addition to that basically simple concept,
trans: 但是，除了这个基本上很简单的概念之外，

name: the bank and its customer owe a large number of obligations to one another.
trans: 这家银行及其客户之间彼此都负有大量的债务。

name: Many of these obligations can give rise to problems and complications but a bank customer, unlike, say, a buyer of goods,
trans: 这些义务中的许多都可能引发问题和复杂情况。但与商品购买者不同，银行客户的情况有所不同……

name: cannot complain that the law is loaded against him.
trans: 不能说法律对他不利（或者说，法律并没有对他造成不公平的对待）。

name: The bank must obey its customer's instructions, and not those of anyone else.
trans: 银行必须遵守客户的指示，而不能听从任何其他人的要求。

name: When, for example, a customer first opens an account, he instructs the bank to debit his account only in respect of cheques drawn by himself.
trans: 例如，当客户首次开设账户时，他会指示银行仅在他自己签发的支票发生支付时才从他的账户中扣款。

name: He gives the bank specimens of his signature, and there is a very firm rule
trans: 他向银行提供了自己的签名样本，而银行有一项非常严格的规定。

name: that the bank has no right or authority to pay out a customer's money on a cheque
trans: 该银行无权也无依据根据客户的支票来支付款项。

name: on which its customer's signature has been forged.
trans: 其上伪造了客户的签名。

name: It makes no difference that the forgery may have been a very skillful one:
trans: 无论这起伪造行为是多么高明（即伪造技术多么精湛），这都无关紧要（即伪造行为的性质并不会因此而改变）。

name: the bank must recognize its customer's signature.
trans: 银行必须确认其客户的签名是真实有效的。

name: For this reason there is no risk to the customer in the practice, adopted by banks, of printing the customer's name on his cheques.
trans: 因此，银行采用在支票上印制客户姓名的做法对客户来说没有任何风险。

name: If this facilitates forgery, it is the bank which will lose, not the customer.
trans: 如果这种做法导致了伪造行为的发生，那么遭受损失的将是银行，而不是客户。

name: The search for oil
trans: 寻找石油的过程

name: What do oilmen want to achieve as soon as they strike oil?
trans: 石油工人一旦发现石油，他们想要实现什么目标呢？

name: The deepest holes of all are made for oil, and they go down to as much as 25, 000 feet.
trans: 所有这些最深的钻孔都是为开采石油而设计的，它们的深度可达25,000英尺。

name: But we do not need to send man down to get the oil out, as we must with other mineral deposits.
trans: 但我们不需要派人下到地下去开采石油；这与开采其他矿产资源的情况不同。

name: The holes are only borings, less than a foot in diameter.
trans: 这些洞只是普通的钻孔，直径不到一英尺。

name: My particular experience is largely in oil, and the search for oil has done more to improve deep drilling than any other mining activity.
trans: 我的主要工作经验集中在石油行业，而在石油勘探领域，寻找石油的过程对深井钻探技术的进步起到了比其他任何采矿活动都更大的推动作用。

name: When it has been decided where we are going to drill,
trans: 一旦我们确定了钻探的位置，

name: we put up at the surface an oil derrick.
trans: 我们在水面上搭建了一座石油钻塔。

name: It has to be tall because it is like a giant block and tackle and we have to lower into the ground
trans: 它必须很高，因为它就像一个巨大的起重设备；我们需要把它降到地面上。

name: and haul out of the ground great lengths of drill pipe which are rotated by an engine at the top
trans: 然后从地下抽出长长的钻杆，这些钻杆由顶部的发动机驱动进行旋转。

name: and are fitted with a cutting bit at the bottom.
trans: 并且底部装有切割刀片。

name: The geologist needs to know what rocks the drill has reached,
trans: 地质学家需要知道钻头已经钻到了哪些类型的岩石上。

name: so every so often a sample is obtained with a coring bit.
trans: 因此，每隔一段时间，就会使用取芯钻头获取一个样本。

name: It cuts a clean cylinder of rock, from which can be seen the strata the drill has been cutting through.
trans: 它切割出了一块整齐的圆柱形岩石，通过这块岩石可以清楚地看到钻头所穿过的岩层结构。

name: Once we get down to the oil, it usually flows to the surface because great pressure either from gas or water, is pushing it.
trans: 一旦石油开始流动，它通常会浮到地表；这是因为气体或水所产生的巨大压力在推动着石油前进。

name: This pressure must be under control, and we control it by means of the mud which we circulate down the drill pipe.
trans: 这种压力必须得到控制，我们通过将泥浆注入钻杆来实现这一目的。

name: We endeavour to avoid the old, romantic idea of a gusher, which wastes oil and gas.
trans: 我们努力摒弃那种过时的、浪漫化的观念——即认为石油和天然气应该被“大量地、无节制地开采”。这种观念实际上会导致资源的浪费。

name: We want it to stay down the hole until we can lead it off in a controlled manner.
trans: 我们希望它一直待在那个洞里，直到我们能够以可控的方式把它引出来。

name: The Butterfly Effect
trans: 蝴蝶效应

name: Why do small errors make it impossible to predict the weather system with a high degree of accuracy?
trans: 为什么微小的误差会导致无法高精度地预测天气系统呢？

name: Beyond two or three days, the world's best weather forecasts are speculative,
trans: 超过两三天之后，世界上最精确的天气预报也就只能算是基于推测的预测结果了。

name: and beyond six or seven they are worthless.
trans: 超过六七个之后，它们就毫无价值了。

name: The Butterfly Effect is the reason.
trans: 这就是“蝴蝶效应”的作用原理。

name: For small pieces of weather--
trans: 对于那些微小的、局部的天气变化（或现象）……

name: and to a global forecaster, small can mean thunderstorms and blizzards--
trans: 对于一位全球气候预测专家来说，“小”这个词汇可能意味着雷暴或暴风雪的来临。

name: any prediction deteriorates rapidly.
trans: 任何预测的结果都会迅速恶化（或：任何预测的准确性都会迅速下降）。

name: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features,
trans: 错误和不确定性不断累积，通过一系列复杂、混乱的环节逐级向上扩散（或：错误与不确定性像级联效应一样，从底层逐渐传递到高层）。

name: from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
trans: 从尘旋和小型风暴，到只有卫星才能观测到的、覆盖整个大陆范围的巨大涡旋……

name: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart,
trans: 现代天气模型使用的是一个由相距约六十英里的点组成的网格系统来进行数据分析和预测。

name: and even so, some starting data has to be guessed,
trans: 即便如此，还是有一些初始数据需要通过猜测来确定的。

name: since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
trans: 因为地面站和卫星无法覆盖所有区域。

name: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart,
trans: 但是，假设地球表面能够被安装上间距为 1 英尺（约 30 厘米）的传感器……

name: rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
trans: 这些粒子以每英尺一英寸的间隔逐渐上升，最终抵达大气的最顶层。

name: Suppose every sensor gives perfectly accurate readings of temperature,
trans: 假设每个传感器都能提供完全准确的温度读数……

name: pressure, humidity, and any other quantity a meteorologist would want.
trans: 压力、湿度，以及气象学家可能需要的任何其他气象参数。

name: Precisely at noon an infinitely powerful computer takes all the data and calculates what will happen at each point
trans: 就在正午时分，一台拥有无限计算能力的计算机会收集所有数据，并预测每个时间点上将会发生什么。

name: at 12.01, then 12.02, then 12.03...
trans: 12点01分，然后是12点02分，接着是12点03分……

name: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
trans: 即使使用了最先进的计算机技术，仍然无法预测一个月后的某一天新泽西州普林斯顿市是否会晴天或下雨。

name: At noon the spaces between the sensors will hide fluctuations that the computer will not know about,
trans: 到了中午时分，传感器之间的间隙会掩盖一些波动现象，而这些波动是计算机无法检测到的。

name: tiny deviations from the average.
trans: 只是与平均值有微小的偏差而已。

name: By 12.01, those fluctuations will already have created small errors one foot away.
trans: 到 12 月 1 日时，这些波动已经会在一英尺之外的位置产生微小的误差（即测量结果出现偏差）。

name: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.
trans: 很快，这些错误将会像病毒一样扩散，其影响范围会扩大到十英尺的尺度，然后继续扩大，最终覆盖整个地球的面积。

name: Secrecy in industry
trans: 行业中的保密性（即信息保密的要求）

name: Why is secrecy particularly important in the chemical industries?
trans: 为什么在化学工业中，保密性尤为重要？

name: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
trans: 有两个因素严重影响了科学研究在工业领域的有效性。

name: One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out,
trans: 其中一点是：整个过程笼罩在一种浓厚的保密氛围之中。

name: the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
trans: 另一方面，还存在着个体研究人员缺乏自由的问题。

name: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one,
trans: 只要任何调查都是保密的（即不对外公开的），

name: it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities,
trans: 这自然会限制所有参与执行这项工作的人与他们所在国家或其他国家的科学家、以及与大学中的科学家进行有效交流的机会。

name: or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
trans: 甚至，这种情况在同一家公司的其他部门中也相当常见。

name: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably.
trans: 保密的程度自然会有很大的差异。

name: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature
trans: 一些大型企业正在进行一些具有普遍性和基础性的研究。

name: that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
trans: 对他们来说，不将这些信息保密反而是一个积极的优势。

name: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.
trans: 然而，许多依赖于此类研究的开发过程都是在完全保密的状态下进行的，直到可以申请专利的阶段才会公开。

name: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
trans: 还有更多的制造工艺根本从未获得专利保护，而是被作为机密工艺严格保密。

name: This applies particularly to chemical industries,
trans: 这尤其适用于化学工业领域。

name: where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
trans: 在那些领域中，偶然的发现所起的作用要比在物理和机械工业中大得多。

name: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
trans: 有时候，保密措施过于严格，以至于根本无法提及这项研究的真正目的或内容。

name: Many firms, for instance have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries
trans: 例如，许多公司在从图书馆获取技术类或科学类书籍时遇到了很大的困难。

name: because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book,
trans: 因为他们不愿意让自己的名字被记录在“借出了某本书”的名单上。

name: for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
trans: 担心其他公司的代理人能够追踪到他们可能正在进行的研究内容。

name: The modern city
trans: 现代城市

name: What is the author's main argument about the modern city?
trans: 作者关于现代城市的主要观点是什么？

name: In the organization of industrial life the influence of the factory upon the physiological and mental state of the workers has been completely neglected.
trans: 在工业生活的组织结构中，工厂对工人生理和心理状态的影响完全被忽视了。

name: Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost,
trans: 现代工业建立在“以最低成本实现最大生产”的理念之上。

name: in order that an individual or a group of individuals may earn as much money as possible.
trans: 这样，个人或某个群体就能赚取尽可能多的钱。

name: It has expanded without any idea of the true nature of the human beings who run the machines,
trans: 它一直在不断扩张，却对那些操控这些机器的人的真实本质一无所知。

name: and without giving any consideration to the effects produced on the individuals and on their descendants by the artificial mode of existence imposed by the factory.
trans: 而且，完全没有考虑到工厂所强加的这种人工生活方式对个人及其后代所产生的影响。

name: The great cities have been built with no regard for us.
trans: 这些伟大的城市是在完全无视我们的存在的情况下建造的。

name: The shape and dimensions of the skyscrapers depend entirely on the necessity of obtaining the maximum income per square foot of ground,
trans: 摩天大楼的形状和尺寸完全取决于实现“每平方英尺土地带来最高收入”这一目标的需要。

name: and of offering to the tenants offices and apartments that please them.
trans: 并且为租户提供他们满意的办公室和公寓。

name: This caused the construction of gigantic buildings where too large masses of human beings are crowded together.
trans: 这导致了巨型建筑物的出现，这些建筑物里挤满了大量的人口。

name: Civilized men like such a way of living.
trans: 文明的人应该喜欢这样的生活方式。

name: While they enjoy the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realize that they are deprived of the necessities of life.
trans: 虽然他们享受着住所带来的舒适与表面的奢华，却未曾意识到自己其实被剥夺了生活所需的基本物资。

name: The modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets full of petrol fumes and toxic gases,
trans: 现代城市由巨大的建筑物以及狭窄、昏暗的街道组成；这些街道里弥漫着汽油烟雾和有毒气体。

name: torn by the noise of the taxicabs, lorries and buses, and thronged ceaselessly by great crowds.
trans: 这里充满了出租车、卡车和公交车的噪音；人群络绎不绝，持续不断地涌来涌去。

name: Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants.
trans: 显然，这一切的规划并非是为了居民们的利益着想。

name: A man-made disease
trans: 一种由人类活动引起的疾病

name: What factor helped to spread the disease of myxomatosis?
trans: 是什么因素导致了黏液瘤病的传播？

name: In the early days of the settlement of Australia, enterprising settlers unwisely introduced the European rabbit.
trans: 在澳大利亚殖民初期，一些富有进取心的移民不慎将欧洲野兔引入了该地区。

name: This rabbit had no natural enemies in the Antipodes, so that it multiplied with that promiscuous abandon characteristic of rabbits.
trans: 这种兔子在南极洲没有天敌，因此它们以兔子特有的繁殖力（即极其旺盛的繁殖能力）大量繁殖。

name: It overran a whole continent.
trans: 它席卷了整个大陆。

name: It caused devastation by burrowing and by devouring the herbage which might have maintained millions of sheep and cattle.
trans: 这种生物通过挖掘洞穴以及啃食本可以养活数百万只羊和牛的牧草，造成了严重的破坏。

name: Scientists discovered that this particular variety of rabbit (and apparently no other animal) was susceptible to a fatal virus disease, myxomatosis.
trans: 科学家发现，这种特定的兔子品种（显然其他动物都没有这种特性）容易感染一种致命的病毒性疾病——黏液瘤病。

name: By infecting animals and letting them loose in the burrows, local epidemics of this disease could be created.
trans: 通过感染动物并将它们放回洞穴中，这种疾病可能会在当地引发流行病。

name: Later it was found that there was a type of mosquito which acted as the carrier of this disease and passed it on to the rabbits.
trans: 后来发现，有一种蚊子是这种疾病的传播媒介，它们将这些病毒传染给了兔子。

name: So while the rest of the world was trying to get rid of mosquitoes, Australia was encouraging this one.
trans: 当世界上其他国家都在努力消灭蚊子时，澳大利亚却在鼓励蚊子的存在。

name: It effectively spread the disease all over the continent and drastically reduced the rabit population.
trans: 这种疾病有效地在整个大陆上蔓延开来，导致兔子的数量急剧减少。

name: It later became apparent that rabbits were developing a degree of resistance to this disease,
trans: 后来发现，兔子对这种疾病逐渐产生了抵抗力。

name: so that the rabbit population was unlikely to be completely exterminated.
trans: 这样一来，兔子种群就不太可能被彻底消灭了。

name: There were hopes, however, that the problem of the rabbit would become manageable.
trans: 然而，人们仍抱有希望，认为这个问题最终是可以得到控制的。

name: Ironically, Europe, which had bequeathed the rabbit as a pest to Australia, acquired this man-made disease as a pestilence.
trans: 具有讽刺意味的是，欧洲将兔子这种害兽引入澳大利亚，结果自己却因此染上了这种由人类活动引发的疾病，并将其视为一种瘟疫。

name: A French physician decided to get rid of the wild rabbits on his own estate and introduced myxomatosis.
trans: 一位法国医生决定清除自己庄园里的野兔，于是他引入了黏液瘤病（myxomatosis）这种病毒来控制野兔的数量。

name: It did not, however, remain within the confines of this estate.
trans: 然而，它并没有停留在这片地产的范围内。

name: It spread through France, where wild rabbits are not generally regarded as a pest but as a sport and a useful food supply,
trans: 这种动物蔓延到了法国。在法国，野兔通常不被视为害兽，而是一种可以用来娱乐的活动对象，同时也是重要的食物来源。

name: and it spread to Britain where wild rabbits are regarded as a pest but where domesticated rabbits,
trans: 这种动物后来传播到了英国。在英国，野兔被视为害兽；而家养的兔子则受到人们的重视（或：在英国，野兔被视为害兽，而家养的兔子则受到人们的喜爱/重视）。

name: equally susceptible to the disease, are the basis of a profitable fur industry.
trans: 这些动物同样容易感染这种疾病，但它们却是利润丰厚的毛皮产业的基础。

name: The question became one of whether Man could control the disease he had invented.
trans: 问题变成了：人类是否能够控制自己所发明的这种疾病。

name: Porpoises
trans: 海豚

name: What would you say is the main characteristic of porpoises?
trans: 你认为海豚的主要特征是什么？

name: There has long been a superstition among mariners that porpoises will save drowning men by pushing them to the surface,
trans: 长期以来，水手们一直有一种迷信：海豚会通过将溺水者推向水面来拯救他们。

name: or protect them from sharks by surrounding them in defensive formation.
trans: 或者通过形成防御阵型来保护它们免受鲨鱼的攻击。

name: Marine Studio biologists have pointed out that, however intelligent they may be,
trans: 海洋生物研究室的生物学家指出，无论这些生物多么聪明，

name: it is probably a mistake to credit dolphins with any motive of life-saving.
trans: 将海豚的行为归因于“拯救生命”的动机，很可能是一种错误的看法。

name: On the occasions when they have pushed to shore an unconscious human being they have much more likely done it out of curiosity or for sport,
trans: 在他们将失去意识的人拖上岸边的那些情况下，他们这么做很可能是出于好奇心或为了寻求刺激（即出于娱乐目的）。

name: as in riding the bow waves of a ship.
trans: 就像乘坐在船的波浪上（即随着船的起伏而移动）一样。

name: In 1928 some porpoises were photographed working like beavers to push ashore a waterlogged mattress.
trans: 1928年，有人拍到了一些海豚正在像海狸一样辛勤地工作，将一个被水浸透的床垫推上岸。

name: If, as has been reported, they have protected humans from sharks,
trans: 如果正如报道所说，它们确实保护了人类免受鲨鱼的攻击，那么……

name: it may have been because curiosity attracted them and because the scent of a possible meal attracted the sharks.
trans: 可能是因为好奇心驱使他们前来，也可能是食物的气味吸引了那些鲨鱼。

name: Porpoises and sharks are natural enemies.
trans: 海豚和鲨鱼是天生的敌人。

name: It is possible that upon such an occasion a battle ensued, with the sharks being driven away or killed.
trans: 在这种情况下，很可能会发生一场战斗：鲨鱼们要么被驱赶走，要么被杀死。

name: Whether it be bird, fish or beast, the porpoise is intrigued with anything that is alive.
trans: 无论是鸟类、鱼类还是其他动物，海豚都对一切有生命的东西都充满好奇心（或：海豚对所有生物都表现出浓厚的兴趣）。

name: They are constantly after the turtles, who peacefully submit to all sorts of indignities.
trans: 他们总是追捕那些海龟，而海龟们则默默地忍受着各种屈辱。

name: One young calf especially enjoyed raising a turtle to the surface with his snout,
trans: 有一只小牛特别喜欢用它的鼻子把海龟顶到水面上。

name: and then shoving him across the tank like an aquaplane.
trans: 然后像推动水上滑板一样把他推过那个水箱。

name: Almost any day a young porpoises may be seen trying to turn a 300-pound sea turtle over by sticking his snout under the edge of his shell and pushing up for dear life.
trans: 几乎每天都能看到小海豚试图将一只重达300磅的海龟翻过来：它们会用鼻子抵住海龟壳的边缘，然后用力向上推。

name: This is not easy, and may require two porpoises working together.
trans: 这并不容易，可能需要两只海豚共同协作才能完成。

name: In another game, as the turtle swims across the oceanarium, the first porpoise swoops down from above and butts his shell with his belly.
trans: 在另一款游戏中，当那只乌龟在海洋馆里游动时，第一只海豚从上方俯冲下来，用它的腹部撞击了乌龟的壳。

name: This knocks the turtle down several feet.
trans: 这一击将那只乌龟击倒了，它摔了好几英尺远。

name: He no sooner recovers his equilibrium than the next porpoises comes along and hits him another crack.
trans: 他刚恢复平衡，下一条鼠海豚就又冲过来，再次击中了他。

name: Eventually the turtle has been butted all the way down to the floor of the tank.
trans: 最终，那只乌龟被挤到了水族箱的底部。

name: He is now satisfied merely to try to stand up, but as soon as he does so a porpoise knocks him flat.
trans: 现在，他仅仅能够尝试站起来就已经感到满足了；然而，他刚一站起来，一只海豚就立刻把他撞倒了。

name: The turtle at last gives up by pulling his feet under his shell and the game is over.
trans: 最后，那只乌龟放弃了尝试，把脚缩进了壳里，游戏也就结束了。

name: The stuff of dreams
trans: 梦中的奥秘

name: What is going on when a person experiences rapid eye-movements during sleep?
trans: 当人在睡眠中经历快速眼动（REM）时，究竟发生了什么？

name: It is fairly clear that the sleeping period must have some function, and because there is so much of it the function would seem to be important.
trans: 很明显，睡眠一定具有某种功能，而且由于这种状态持续的时间很长，因此这种功能必定非常重要。

name: Speculations about its nature have been going on for literally thousands of years,
trans: 关于睡眠本质的猜测已经持续了数千年之久。

name: and one odd finding that makes the problem puzzling is that it looks very much as if sleeping is not simply a matter of giving the body a rest.
trans: 一个令人困惑的现象是：睡眠似乎并不仅仅是让身体休息的过程。

name: 'Rest', in terms of muscle relaxation and so on, can be achieved by a brief period lying, or even sitting down.
trans: 从肌肉放松的角度来看，即使只是短暂地躺下或坐着，也能达到休息的效果。

name: The body's tissues are self-repairing and self-restoring to a degree, and function best when more or less continuously active.
trans: 人体组织本身具备自我修复和恢复的功能，而且在保持一定程度的活动状态下，其功能才能达到最佳状态。

name: In fact a basic amount of movement occurs during sleep which is specifically concerned with preventing muscle inactivity.
trans: 事实上，睡眠期间确实会发生一些活动，这些活动专门用于防止肌肉长时间处于静止状态。

name: If it is not a question of resting the body, then perhaps it is the brain that needs resting?
trans: 如果睡眠的目的不是为了让身体休息，那么或许大脑才是需要休息的对象？

name: This might be a plausible hypothesis were it not for two factors.
trans: 这个假设听起来似乎合理，但有两个因素需要考虑：

name: First the electroencephalograph (which is simply a device for recording the electrical activity of the brain by attaching electrodes to the scalp)
trans: 首先，脑电图（EEG）是一种通过将电极贴在头皮上来记录大脑电活动的设备……

name: shows that while there is a change in the pattern of activity during sleep,
trans: 研究表明，虽然睡眠期间的活动模式会发生变化，

name: there is no evidence that the total amount of activity is any less.
trans: 没有证据表明总体活动量有任何减少。

name: The second factor is more interesting and more fundamental.
trans: 第二个因素更加有趣，也更为根本。

name: Some years ago an American psychiatrist named William Dement published experiments dealing with the recording of eye-movements during sleep.
trans: 几年前，一位名叫威廉·德门特（William Dement）的美国精神病学家发表了一项研究，该研究记录了人们在睡眠期间的眼球运动情况。

name: He showed that the average individual's sleep cycle is punctuated with peculiar bursts of eye-movements, some drifting and slow, others jerky and rapid.
trans: 他发现，普通人的睡眠周期中会伴随着一些特殊的眼球运动现象：有些眼球运动较为缓慢、平稳，而另一些则突然、快速地发生。

name: People woken during these periods of eye-movements generally reported that they had been dreaming.
trans: 在眼球运动期间被唤醒的人通常报告说他们正在做梦。

name: When woken at other times they reported no dreams.
trans: 在其他时间被唤醒时，他们表示自己没有做任何梦。

name: If one group of people were disturbed from their eye-movement sleep for several nights on end,
trans: 如果有一组人的眼球运动睡眠（REM sleep）连续几个晚上都被中断的话……

name: and another group were disturbed for an equal period of time but when they were not exhibiting eye-movements,
trans: 另一组实验对象也被同样长的时间所干扰，但在这段时间里他们并没有表现出任何眼球运动（即他们的目光没有发生任何移动）。

name: the first group began to show some personality disorders while the others seemed more or less unaffected.
trans: 第一组开始出现一些人格障碍的症状，而其他组则几乎没有受到影响。

name: The implications of all this were that it was not the disturbance of sleep that mattered, but the disturbance of dreaming.
trans: 所有这些现象表明，真正重要的是睡眠本身的中断，而不是梦境本身的中断。

name: Snake poison
trans: 蛇毒

name: What are the two different ways in which snake poison acts?
trans: 蛇毒的作用方式主要有哪两种？

name: How in came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
trans: 蛇为何会进化出毒液，这仍然是个谜。

name: Over the periods their saliva, a mild, digestive juice like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.
trans: 随着时间的推移，它们唾液中的成分——原本只是类似我们人体消化液的温和物质——逐渐演变成了至今仍难以解析的毒液。

name: It was not forced upon them by the survival competition;
trans: 这种毒液的产生并非出于生存竞争的必然；

name: they could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
trans: 即使没有毒液，蛇也能通过捕猎获得食物（就像如今数以千计的无毒蛇一样）。

name: Poison to a snake is merely a luxury;
trans: 对蛇来说，毒液其实是一种“奢侈品”；

name: it enables it to get its food with very little effort, no more effort than one bite.
trans: 它让蛇能够毫不费力地捕获猎物，只需轻轻一咬即可。

name: And why only snakes?
trans: 那么，为什么只有蛇会拥有毒液呢？

name: Cats, for instance, would be greatly helped;
trans: 以猫为例，毒液对它们来说同样大有帮助：

name: no running fights with large, fierce rats or tussles with grown rabbits--just a bite and no more effort needed.
trans: 它们无需与大型凶猛的老鼠搏斗，也不必与成年兔子缠斗——只需一口咬下，就能轻松取胜。

name: In fact, it would be an assistance to all carnivores though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.
trans: 事实上，这对所有食肉动物来说都是一种帮助；不过当它们互相争斗时，这也会成为一把“双刃剑”（即既有利也有弊）。

name: But, of the vertebrates unpredictable Nature selected only snakes (and one lizard).
trans: 但是，在这些脊椎动物中，不可预测的自然法则只选择了蛇（以及一种蜥蜴）作为进化成功的物种。

name: One wonders also why Nature, with some snakes concocted poison of such extreme potency.
trans: 人们也会不禁疑惑：为什么大自然会赋予某些蛇类如此剧毒的毒液呢？

name: In the conversion of saliva into poison, one might suppose that a fixed process took place. It did not;
trans: 在将唾液转化为毒物的过程中，人们可能会认为这个过程是固定不变的（即每次转化都遵循相同的步骤或机制）。但实际上并非如此。

name: some snakes manufactured a poison different in every respect from that of others,
trans: 有些蛇产生的毒液在各个方面都与其他蛇产生的毒液不同。

name: as different as arsenic is from strychnine, and having different effects.
trans: 就像砷和士的宁截然不同一样，这两种物质也具有不同的作用（或效果）。

name: One poison acts on the nerves, the other on the blood.
trans: 一种毒物作用于神经系统，另一种则作用于血液。

name: The makers of the nerve poison include the mambas and the cobras and their venom is called neurotoxic.
trans: 制造这种神经毒素的动物包括曼巴蛇和眼镜蛇，它们的毒液被称为神经毒素（neurotoxic venom）。

name: Vipers (adders) and rattlesnakes manufacture the blood poison, which is known as haemolytic.
trans: 蝰蛇和响尾蛇会分泌一种血液毒素，这种毒素被称为“溶血毒素”（haemolytic toxin）。

name: Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.
trans: 这两种毒药都很危险、令人不适，但其中毒性更强、危害更大的无疑是“血液毒药”。

name: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
trans: 据说，这种神经毒素是两者中较为原始的类型；而血液毒素则可以看作是一种通过改进配方而开发出来的“新型产品”。

name: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
trans: 尽管如此，这种神经毒素对人体的影响速度要比血液毒素快得多。

name: This, however, means nothing.
trans: 然而，这其实毫无意义。

name: Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man but for use against prey such as rats and mice,
trans: 蛇之所以拥有毒液，并不是为了用来对付人类，而是为了捕杀老鼠等猎物。

name: and the effects on these of viperine poison is almost immediate.
trans: 毒蛇的毒液对这些生物的影响几乎是立竿见影的。

name: William S.Hart and the early 'Western' film
trans: 威廉·S·哈特与早期的“西部片”
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: How did William Hart's childhood prepare him for his acting role in Western films?
trans: 威廉·哈特的童年经历是如何为他日后在西部电影中扮演演员角色奠定基础的？
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: William S.Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars,
trans: 威廉·S·哈特或许是有史以来最伟大的西方明星。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
trans: 与加里·库珀（Gary Cooper）和约翰·韦恩（John Wayne）不同，他只出演过西部片（Westerns）。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: From 1914 to 1924 he was supreme and unchallenged.
trans: 从 1914 年到 1924 年，他一直是无可争议的领袖，无人能够与他竞争。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film,
trans: 正是哈特创造了西方电影的基本公式。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made,
trans: 并且为他自己在每一部电影中扮演的角色精心设计了形象（即设计了角色的性格、外貌、行为方式等）。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: the good-bad man, the accidental, noble outlaw,
trans: 这个“好与坏并存”的人，这个既是意外产物、又具有高尚品质的亡命之徒……
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: or the honest, but framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip;
trans: 或者是那个诚实却被诬陷的牛仔，又或者是那个因恶毒的谣言而受到怀疑的警长……
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
trans: 简而言之，这个人正处于与自己以及周围环境（即“边界环境”）的冲突之中。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Unlike most of his contemporaries in Hollywood,
trans: 与好莱坞的大多数同时代人不同，
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Hart actually knew something of the old West.
trans: 哈特其实对美国西部历史有所了解。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing,
trans: 他小时候就生活在那里，那时西部文明已逐渐消逝；
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences,
trans: 他的英雄形象深深植根于他的记忆与经历之中，
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier,
trans: 以及那片消失的边疆的历史与传说之中。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized,
trans: 尽管美国历史上没有哪个时期或地点被如此荒谬地浪漫化了，
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena,
trans: 但在至少一点上，神话与现实确实交汇在了一起——
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
trans: 那就是个人与不断扩张的文明之间的冲突。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Men accustomed to struggling for survival against the elements and Indians
trans: 那些习惯了与自然环境及印第安人抗争以求生存的人们，
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: were bewildered by politicians, bankers and businessmen,
trans: 却被政客、银行家和商人搞得无所适从；
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: and unhorsed by fences, laws and alien taboos.
trans: 那些不受束缚的人，被围栏、法律以及陌生的禁忌所束缚。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Hart's good-bad man was always an outsider, always one of the disinherited,
trans: 哈特笔下的那些“好人与坏人”始终是局外人，始终是被社会抛弃的人；
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: and if he found it necessary to shoot a sheriff or rob a bank along the way,
trans: 如果他觉得有必要开枪打死警长或抢劫银行，他也会这么做。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: his early audiences found it easy to understand and forgive,
trans: 他的早期观众觉得这些内容很容易理解，也愿意原谅其中的不足之处。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: especially when it was Hart who, in the end, overcame the attacking Indians.
trans: 尤其是当最终是哈特（Hart）击败了那些进攻力强劲的印第安人队（Indians）的时候。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Audiences in the second decade of the twentieth century
trans: 二十世纪第二个十年的观众群体
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: found it pleasant to escape to a time when life, though hard, was relatively simple.
trans: 我觉得回到那个虽然生活艰难但相对简单的时代是一种令人愉悦的体验。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy,
trans: 我们至今仍在面对这些问题：生活在一个充满隐秘的敌意、战争、虚伪与欺骗的世界里……
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives,
trans: 欺诈、混乱以及即将到来的毁灭，都是我们日常生活的一部分。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: we all want a code to live by.
trans: 我们都希望有一套可以遵循的准则或规则来指导我们的行为。
lesson: NCE4 · William S. Hart and the Early "Western" Film

name: Knowledge and progress
trans: 知识与进步

name: In what two areas have people made no 'progress' at all?
trans: 在哪些两个领域，人们完全没有取得任何进展？

name: Why does the idea of progress loom so large in the modern world?
trans: 为什么“进步”的概念在现代社会中显得如此重要（或者说，为什么人们对“进步”的追求如此强烈）？

name: Surely because progress of a particular kind is actually taking place around us
trans: 肯定是因为某种形式的进步正在我们周围实实在在地发生着。

name: and is becoming more and more manifest.
trans: 而且这种现象正变得越来越明显（或：这种现象正逐渐变得清晰可见）。

name: Although mankind has undergone no general improvement in intelligence or morality,
trans: 尽管人类的智力或道德水平并没有普遍性的提升，

name: it has made extraordinary progress in the accumulation of knowledge.
trans: 在知识的积累方面，它取得了非凡的进展。

name: Knowledge began to increase as soon as the thoughts of one individual
trans: 一旦某个人的思想开始被记录或传播，知识就开始不断积累（即知识量开始增加）。

name: could be communicated to another by means of speech.
trans: 可以通过语言的方式传达给另一个人。

name: With the invention of writing, a great advance was made,
trans: 随着文字的发明，人类社会取得了巨大的进步。

name: for knowledge could then be not only communicated but also stored.
trans: 这样一来，知识不仅可以被传播，还可以被储存起来。

name: Libraries made education possible, and education in its turn added to libraries:
trans: 图书馆使教育成为可能，而教育又反过来促进了图书馆的发展（即促进了图书馆资源的丰富与建设）。

name: the growth of knowledge followed a kind of compound interest law,
trans: 知识的增长遵循了一种类似于“复利”的规律。

name: which was greatly enhanced by the invention of printing.
trans: 这一情况因印刷术的发明而得到了极大的改善。

name: All this was comparatively slow until, with the coming of science,
trans: 在科学出现之前，所有这些发展都相对缓慢。

name: the tempo was suddenly raised.
trans: 节奏突然加快了。

name: Then knowledge began to be accumulated according to a systematic plan.
trans: 于是，知识开始按照系统的计划被逐步积累起来。

name: The trickle became a stream: the stream has now become a torrent.
trans: 起初只是细小的水流，后来逐渐汇聚成了一条小溪；如今，这条小溪已经变成了湍急的急流。

name: Moreover, as soon as new knowledge is acquired, it is now turned to practical account.
trans: 此外，一旦获得了新的知识，就会立即将其应用于实际中。

name: What is called 'modern civilization'
trans: 所谓的“现代文明”究竟是什么？

name: is not the result of a balanced development of all man's nature,
trans: 这并不是人类所有天性得到平衡发展的结果。

name: but of accumulated knowledge applied to practical life.
trans: 而是将积累的知识应用于实际生活中。

name: The problem now facing humanity is:
trans: 人类现在面临的问题是：

name: What is going to be done with all this knowledge?
trans: 这些知识将会被用来做什么呢？

name: As is so often pointed out, knowledge is a two-edged weapon
trans: 正如人们经常指出的那样，知识是一把双刃剑。

name: which can be used equally for good or evil.
trans: 这种技术既可以用于善，也可以用于恶。

name: It is now being used indifferently for both.
trans: 现在，它被随意地用于这两种用途（或：现在，它被不加区分地用于这两种情况）。

name: Could any spectacle, for instance, be more grimly whimsical
trans: 比如说，还有哪种场景能比这更加荒诞、又充满阴郁的幽默感呢？

name: than that of gunners using science to shatter men's bodies
trans: 这比那些利用科学手段摧毁人类身体的炮手们所做的还要可怕。

name: while, close at hand, surgeons use it to restore them?
trans: 那么，当外科医生就在眼前、可以使用这种技术来帮助患者恢复健康时，为什么还要犹豫呢？

name: We have to ask ourselves very seriously
trans: 我们必须非常严肃地问自己一个问题。

name: what will happen if this twofold use of knowledge,
trans: 如果这种对知识的双重利用方式得以实现，将会发生什么呢？

name: with its ever-increasing power, continues.
trans: 随着其不断增长的能量，这一过程持续进行着。

name: Bird flight
trans: 鸟类的飞行

name: What are the two main types of bird flight described by the author?
trans: 作者描述了哪两种主要的鸟类飞行方式？

name: No two sorts of birds practise quite the same sort of flight;
trans: 没有两种鸟类的飞行方式是完全相同的。

name: the varieties are infinite; but two classes may be roughly seen.
trans: 虽然种类繁多、无穷无尽，但大致上可以分为两类。

name: Any ship that crosses the Pacific
trans: 任何横渡太平洋的船只

name: is accompanied for many days by the smaller albatross,
trans: 在许多天里，它都伴随着那只体型较小的信天翁。

name: which may keep company with the vessel for an hour
trans: 这艘船可能会与另一艘船一起航行一个小时。

name: without visible or more than occasional movement of wing.
trans: 翅膀没有明显的运动，或者仅有偶尔的轻微摆动。

name: The currents of air that the walls of the ship direct upwards,
trans: 那些被船体墙壁引导向上的气流……

name: as well as in the line of its course,
trans: 以及按照其发展的自然规律（或：按照其既定的方向/进程）。

name: are enough to give the great bird with its immense wings
trans: 这些（资源或条件）足以让那只拥有巨大翅膀的巨鸟翱翔天际。

name: sufficient sustenance and progress.
trans: 充足的生活保障与持续的发展。

name: The albatross is the king of the gliders,
trans: 信天翁是滑翔鸟类中的“王者”。

name: the class of fliers which harness the air to their purpose,
trans: 这类飞行器能够利用空气来达到它们的目的。

name: but must yield to its opposition.
trans: 但它最终必须屈服于自己的对手（或反对者）。

name: In the contrary school, the duck is supreme.
trans: 在另一种观点中，鸭子才是至高无上的存在。

name: It comes nearer to the engines with which man has 'conquered' the air, as he boasts.
trans: 它越来越接近那些人类用来“征服”天空的飞行器了——正如人类所自豪地宣称的那样。

name: Duck, and like them the pigeons, are endowed with steel-like muscles,
trans: 鸭子，和鸽子一样，拥有像钢铁一样强健的肌肉。

name: that are a good part of the weight of the bird,
trans: 这些部分占据了鸟类体重的很大比例。

name: and these will ply the short wings with such irresistible power
trans: 这些装置将会以一种极其强大的力量驱动那些短小的翅膀（即那些用于飞行的结构）。

name: that they can bore for long distances through an opposing gale
trans: 它们能够在强风的阻碍下仍持续前进（或：它们能够在强风的冲击下继续长距离移动）。

name: before exhaustion follows.
trans: 在精疲力竭随之而来之前……

name: Their humbler followers, such as partridges,
trans: 他们那些地位较低的追随者，比如鹧鸪之类的动物……

name: have a like power of strong propulsion, but soon tire.
trans: 它们拥有强大的推进力，但很快就会疲劳。

name: You may pick them up in utter exhaustion,
trans: 即使它们在极度疲惫的状态下被我们捡起，

name: if wind over the sea has driven them to a long journey.
trans: 也可能是因为海上的风将它们驱使进行了漫长的旅程。

name: The swallow shares the virtues of both schools in highest measure.
trans: 燕子完美地结合了这两种特性的优点：

name: It tires not, nor does it boast of its power; but belongs to the air
trans: 它不会感到疲劳，也不会夸耀自己的力量；

name: travelling it may be six thousand miles to and from its northern nesting home,
trans: 它属于天空，可以往返于数千英里外的北方巢穴之间，

name: feeding its flown young as it flies, and slipping through a medium
trans: 在飞行中为幼鸟提供食物，

name: that seems to help its passage even when the wind is adverse.
trans: 并且能够轻松穿过各种环境——即使风势逆境也是如此。

name: Such birds do us good,
trans: 这样的鸟类对我们有益；

name: though we no longer take omens from their flight on this side and that;
trans: 尽管如今我们不再从它们的飞行中寻找预兆；

name: and even the most superstitious villagers no longer take off their hats to the magpie and wish it good-morning.
trans: 就连最迷信的村民，也不会再向喜鹊脱帽致以问候了。

name: Beauty
trans: 美丽

name: What do glimpses of beauty, either in nature or art, often suggest to the human mind?
trans: 无论是自然界中的美景，还是艺术作品中的美感，它们往往能给人类的心灵带来怎样的启示呢？

name: A young man sees a sunset and,
trans: 一个年轻人看到了日落，

name: unable to understand or to express the emotion that it rouses in him,
trans: 无法理解这种情感在他心中所引发的反应，也无法表达出自己所感受到的情绪。

name: concludes that it must be the gateway to a world that lies beyond
trans: 得出结论：这一定是通往另一个未知世界的入口。

name: It is difficult for any of us in moments of intense aesthetic experience
trans: 在那些充满强烈审美体验的时刻，对我们任何人来说都很难做到（保持冷静或理性）。

name: to resist the suggestion that we are catching a glimpse of a light
trans: （用于反驳“我们似乎瞥见了某种光芒”的说法）

name: that shines down to us from a different realm of existence, different and,
trans: 那种光芒是从另一个存在领域照射到我们这里的；那个领域与我们截然不同……

name: because the experience is intensely moving, in some way higher.
trans: 因为这种体验非常令人感动，从某种意义上来说，它的价值甚至更高（即这种体验带来的意义或影响更为深远）。

name: And, though the gleams blind and dazzle, yet do they convey a hint of beauty and serenity
trans: 尽管那些光芒刺眼、令人眩目，但它们依然透露出一种美丽与宁静的气息。

name: greater than we have known or imagined. Greater too than we can describe;
trans: 比我们以往所知道或想象的都要伟大；同时也超出了我们的描述能力。

name: for language, which was invented to convey the meanings of this world
trans: 对于这种语言来说——它被创造出来就是为了传达这个世界的意义——它很难被直接应用于其他目的。

name: cannot readily be fitted to the uses of another.
trans: 所有伟大的艺术都具有这种能力：能够暗示一个超越现实的世界。这一点是不可否认的。

name: That all great art has this power of suggesting a world beyond is undeniable.
trans: 在某些时刻，大自然本身也具备这种能力。

name: In some moods, nature shares it.
trans: 六月的天空再蓝，也不会不让人期待更加湛蓝的天空；

name: There is no sky in June so blue that it does not point forward to a bluer,
trans: 再美的日落，也不会不唤起人们对更美好事物的向往；

name: no sunset so beautiful that it does not waken the vision of a greater beauty,
trans: 然而，这种美好往往在人们尚未完全看清之前就消失了，

name: a vision which passes before it is fully glimpsed,
trans: 只留下一种难以言喻的渴望与遗憾。

name: and in passing leaves an indefinable longing and regret.
trans: 但是，如果这个世界不仅仅是一个糟糕的玩笑，

name: But, if this world is not merely a bad joke,
trans: 如果生命不是在星辰冷冽光芒中的短暂闪光，

name: life a vulgar flare amid the cool radiance of the stars,
trans: 如果存在不是对那些神秘事物的徒劳嘲笑……

name: and existence an empty laugh braying across the mysteries;
trans: 那么，这些关于“背后、超越这个世界的事物”的暗示，

name: if these intimations of a something behind and beyond
trans: 就一定有着更深层的意义。

name: are not evil humour born of indigestion,
trans: 这些幽默并不是由消化不良引起的（即：这些幽默并非源于身体不适或情绪低落）。

name: or whimsies sent by the devil to mock and madden us, if, in a word
trans: 又或者是魔鬼为了嘲笑和折磨我们而派来的种种怪念头（或奇想）……总之，就是这些无法解释的事情。

name: beauty means something yet we must not seek to interpret the meaning.
trans: “美”确实蕴含着某种意义，但我们却不应试图去解读这种意义。

name: If we glimpse the unutterable, it is unwise to try to utter it,
trans: 如果我们试图去表达那些无法用语言表达的事物，那无疑是愚蠢的。

name: nor should we seek to invest with significance that which we cannot grasp.
trans: 我们也不应该试图投资那些我们无法理解、无法掌握其本质的事物。

name: Beauty in terms of our human meanings is meaningless.
trans: 从人类的角度来看，“美”这个概念本身是没有意义的（即“美”并没有实质性的、可以定义的价值或意义）。

name: Non-auditory effects of noise
trans: 噪声的非听觉影响

name: What conclusion does the author draw about noise and health in this piece?
trans: 作者在这篇文章中关于“噪音与健康”得出了什么结论？

name: Many people in industry and the Services,
trans: 许多来自工业界和服务行业的人士……

name: who have practical experience of noise,
trans: 那些具有处理噪声问题实际经验的人

name: regard any investigation of this question as a waste of time;
trans: 认为对这个问题进行任何调查都是浪费时间；

name: they are not prepared even to admit the possibility that noise affects people.
trans: 他们甚至不愿意承认“噪音会影响人们”这一可能性。

name: On the other hand,
trans: 另一方面，

name: those who dislike noise will sometimes use most inadequate evidence
trans: 那些不喜欢噪音的人，有时会使用极其不充分的论据（或证据）来支持自己的观点。

name: to support their pleas for a quieter society.
trans: 以支持他们关于营造一个更加宁静社会的诉求。

name: This is a pity, because noise abatement really is a good cause,
trans: 这真是太遗憾了，因为减少噪音确实是一个非常有益的事业（或：减少噪音是一件很有意义的事情）。

name: and it is likely to be discredited if it gets to be associated with bad science.
trans: 如果这种理论或方法与糟糕的科学实践（即不严谨、不科学的研究方法）联系在一起，它很可能会被人们质疑或否定（即失去可信度）。

name: One allegation often made is that noise produces mental illness.
trans: 一个常见的指控是：噪音会导致精神疾病。

name: A recent article in a weekly newspaper, for instance,
trans: 例如，最近一家周刊上发表了一篇文章……

name: was headed with a striking illustration of a lady in a state of considerable distress,
trans: 这本书的封面配有一幅引人注目的插图，描绘了一位处于极度困境中的女士。

name: with the caption 'She was yet another victim, reduced to a screaming wreck'.
trans: 配文写道：“她只是又一个受害者，被折磨得痛苦不堪、尖叫连连。”

name: On turning eagerly to the text, one learns that the lady was a typist
trans: 当人们急切地阅读这段文字时，会发现那位女士原来是一名打字员。

name: who found the sound of office typewriters worried her more and more
trans: 谁发现了办公室里打字机的声音？这个发现让她越来越感到担忧。

name: until eventually she had to go into a mental hospital.
trans: 直到最后，她不得不被送进精神病院。

name: Now the snag in this sort of anecdote is of course that one cannot distinguish cause and effect.
trans: 当然，这类轶事的一个问题在于人们无法区分其中的因果关系（即哪些事件是原因，哪些是结果）。

name: Was the noise a cause of the illness,
trans: 这种噪音是导致疾病的原因吗？

name: or were the complaints about noise merely a symptom?
trans: 还是说，那些关于噪音的投诉只不过是问题的一个表面现象（即真正的问题隐藏在更深层次呢？）

name: Another patient might equally well complain
trans: 另一个患者也很可能会提出同样的抱怨。

name: that her neighbours were combining to slander her and persecute her,
trans: 她的邻居们联合起来诽谤她、迫害她。

name: and yet one might be cautious about believing this statement.
trans: 然而，人们或许会对这一说法持谨慎态度（即不太相信它）。

name: What is needed in the case of noise is a study of large numbers of people living under noisy conditions,
trans: 在噪声环境下，我们需要对大量生活在嘈杂环境中的人进行研究。

name: to discover whether they are mentally ill more often than other people are.
trans: 为了查明他们是否比普通人更容易患上精神疾病。

name: Some time ago the United States Navy, for instance,
trans: 例如，不久前美国海军就……

name: examined a very large number of men working on aircraft carriers:
trans: 对大量在航空母舰上工作的男性进行了检查。

name: the study was known as Project Anehin.
trans: 这项研究被称为“Project Anehin”。

name: It can be unpleasant to live even several miles from an aerodrome;
trans: 即使住在距离机场几英里远的地方，生活也可能很不方便（或：生活质量可能会受到影响）。

name: if you think what it must be like to share the deck of a ship with several squadrons of jet aircraft,
trans: 如果你想象一下：与几支喷气式飞机中队共享同一艘船的甲板，那会是什么样子……

name: you will realize that a modern navy is a good place to study noise.
trans: 你会发现，现代海军是一个研究噪声问题的理想场所。

name: But neither psychiatric interviews nor objective tests
trans: 但是，无论是心理评估访谈还是客观测试，都无法提供准确的结果。

name: were able to show any effects upon these American sailors.
trans: 他们未能证明这些措施对这些美国水手有任何实际影响（或：他们未能证明这些措施对这些美国水手产生了任何积极或消极的效果）。

name: This result merely confirms earlier American and British studies:
trans: 这一结果仅仅证实了此前美国和英国的研究结果而已。

name: if there is any effect of noise upon mental health,
trans: 如果噪音对心理健康有任何影响的话……

name: it must be so small that present methods of psychiatric diagnosis cannot find it.
trans: 它一定非常微小，以至于现有的精神疾病诊断方法无法检测到它。

name: That does not prove that it does not exist; but it does mean
trans: 这并不能证明该事物根本不存在；不过这确实意味着……

name: that noise is less dangerous than, say being brought up in an orphanage
trans: 那种噪音其实没有在孤儿院长大的情况那么危险（或者说，那种噪音的危害要小得多）。

name: --which really is a mental health hazard.
trans: 这确实对心理健康构成了威胁。

name: The past life of the earth
trans: 地球的过去生命
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: What is the main condition for the preservation of the remains of any living creature?
trans: 保存任何生物遗骸的主要条件是什么？
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: It is animals and plants which lived in or near water whose remains are most likely to be preserved,
trans: 最有可能被保存下来的，是那些生活在水中或水边的动植物的遗骸。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: for one of the necessary conditions of preservation is quick burial,
trans: 其中一个必要的保存条件就是迅速掩埋。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: and it is only in the seas and rivers, and sometimes lakes,
trans: 而这些生物只存在于海洋、河流中，偶尔也会出现在湖泊里。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: where mud and silt have been continuously deposited,
trans: 在那些泥沙不断沉积的地方……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: that bodies and the like can be rapidly covered over and preserved.
trans: 那些尸体之类的东西可以被迅速覆盖起来并加以保存。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: But even in the most favourable circumstances
trans: 但即使在最有利的情况下
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: only a small fraction of the creatures that die are preserved in this way
trans: 只有极少数死亡的生物能够以这种方式被保存下来。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: before decay sets in or, even more likely, before scavengers eat them.
trans: 在腐烂开始之前，或者更有可能的是，在那些以腐肉为食的生物（如食腐动物）将它们吃掉之前。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: After all, all living creatures live by feeding on something else,
trans: 毕竟，所有生物都是通过摄取其他物质来维持生存的。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: whether it be plant or animal, dead or alive,
trans: 无论是植物还是动物，无论是死的还是活的……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: and it is only by chance that such a fate is avoided.
trans: 只有偶然的情况下，这样的命运才能被避免。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: The remains of plants and animals that lived on land are much more rarely preserved,
trans: 生活在陆地上的植物和动物的遗骸被保存下来的情况要少得多。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: for there is seldom anything to cover them over.
trans: 因为通常没有什么东西可以用来遮盖它们（即那些需要被遮盖的东西）。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about,
trans: 当你想到那些在空中飞舞的无数鸟类时……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles which you do not see,
trans: 更不用说那些数量同样众多的小型动物了，比如田鼠和鼩鼱——它们是肉眼看不见的。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.
trans: 很少有人会偶然发现尸体，当然，路边除外。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: They decompose and are quickly destroyed by the weather or eaten by some other creature.
trans: 它们会分解，并很快被天气因素破坏，或者被其他生物吃掉。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: It is almost always due to some very special circumstances that traces of land animals survive,
trans: 几乎总是由于一些非常特殊的情况，陆地动物的痕迹才能得以保存下来。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: as by falling into inaccessible caves, or into an ice crevasse,
trans: 比如掉进无法进入的洞穴里，或者掉进冰裂隙里。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: like the Siberian mammoths,
trans: 就像西伯利亚猛犸象一样……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: when the whole animal is sometimes preserved, as in a refrigerator.
trans: 当整个动物被保存下来时（例如被存放在冰箱中），这种情况也是存在的。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: This is what happened to the famous Beresovka mammoth which was found preserved and in good condition.
trans: 这就是著名的贝列索夫卡猛犸象的遭遇：它被发现时保存完好，状态极佳。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: In his mouth were the remains of fir trees--the last meal that he had before he fell into the crevasse and broke his back.
trans: 他的嘴里残留着冷杉的枝叶——那是他在掉进裂缝、摔断脊椎之前的最后一餐。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: The mammoth has now been restored in the Palaeontological Museum in St.Petersburg.
trans: 这头猛犸象现已被修复并陈列在圣彼得堡的古生物博物馆中。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: Other animals were trapped in tar pits, like the elephants, sabre-toothed cats,
trans: 其他动物也陷入了沥青坑中，比如大象和剑齿虎。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: and numerous other creatures that are found at Rancho la Brea, which is now just a suburb of Los Angeles.
trans: 以及许多其他生物，它们都生活在拉布里亚牧场（Rancho la Brea）——如今这个地方已经成为了洛杉矶的一个郊区。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: Apparently what happened was that water collected on these tar pits
trans: 显然，发生的情况是水在这些沥青坑中积聚了。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: and the bigger animals like the elephants ventured out on to the apparently firm surface to drink,
trans: 那些体型较大的动物，比如大象，便冒险走到了那片看起来非常坚固的地面上去喝水。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: and were promptly bogged in the tar.
trans: 结果他们立刻陷入了困境（或：陷入了麻烦）。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: And then, when they were dead, the carnivores,
trans: 然后，当它们死去之后，那些肉食动物……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: like the sabretoothed cats and the giant wolves,
trans: 就像剑齿虎和巨型狼一样……
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: came out to feed and suffered exactly the same fate.
trans: 它们出来觅食，结果遭遇了完全相同的命运。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: There are also endless numbers of birds in the tar as well.
trans: 在沥青中也有数不清的鸟儿。
lesson: NCE4 · The Past Life of the Earth

name: The 'Vasa'
trans: “瓦萨号”

name: What happened to the 'Vasa' almost immediately after she was launched?
trans: “瓦萨号”在下水后几乎立刻就发生了什么？

name: From the seventeenth-century empire of Sweden,
trans: 从十七世纪的瑞典帝国开始……

name: the story of a galleon that sank at the start of her maiden voyage in 1628 must be one of the strangest tales of the sea.
trans: 这艘加莱昂帆船的故事堪称海洋史上最离奇的传说之一：它在1628年首次航行时便沉没了。

name: For nearly three and a half centuries she lay at the bottom of Stockholm harbour until her discovery in 1956.
trans: 在将近三个半世纪的时间里，这艘船一直沉躺在斯德哥尔摩港的底部，直到1956年才被人发现。

name: This was the Vasa, royal flagship of the great imperial fleet.
trans: 这艘船是“瓦萨号”（Vasa），属于那个伟大帝国舰队的皇家旗舰。

name: King Gustavus Adolphus 'The Northern Hurricane',
trans: 古斯塔夫·阿道夫国王，被称为“北方飓风”……

name: then at the height of his military success in the 'Thirty Years' War,
trans: 就在他在“三十年战争”中取得军事胜利的巅峰时期，

name: had dictated her measurements and armament.
trans: 她已经将自己的身体尺寸以及所携带的武器（或装备）详细记录了下来。

name: Triple gun-decks mounted sixty-four bronze cannon.
trans: 三层甲板上共安装了六十四门青铜大炮。

name: She was intended to play a leading role in the growing might of Sweden.
trans: 她原本被期望在瑞典日益强大的过程中扮演核心领导角色。

name: As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August 10, 1628, Stockholm was in a ferment.
trans: 1628年8月10日，当这艘船准备进行它的首航时，斯德哥尔摩正处于一片动荡之中。

name: From the Skeppsbron and surrounding islands
trans: 从斯凯普斯布隆（Skeppsbron）以及周围的岛屿出发

name: the people watched this thing of beauty begin to spread her sails and catch the wind.
trans: 人们看着这艘美丽的船开始扬起帆，迎风启航。

name: They had laboured for three years to produce this floating work of art;
trans: 他们花了三年时间才完成这件浮动的艺术品。

name: she was more richly carved and ornamented than any previous ship.
trans: 它的雕刻和装饰比以往任何一艘船都要精美、复杂得多。

name: The high stern castle was a riot of carved gods, demons, knights, kings, warriors,
trans: 那座高耸在船尾的城堡上，雕刻着各式各样的神祇、恶魔、骑士、国王以及战士的形象；整个墙面仿佛是一场视觉的狂欢盛宴。

name: mermaids, cherubs; and zoomorphic animal shapes ablaze with red and gold and blue,
trans: 美人鱼、小天使，以及那些被红色、金色和蓝色装饰得绚丽多彩的动物形状……

name: symbols of courage, power, and cruelty,
trans: 象征着勇气、力量与残酷的符号……

name: were portrayed to stir the imaginations of the superstitious sailors of the day.
trans: 这些描述被用来激发当时那些迷信的水手的想象力。

name: Then the cannons of the anchored warships thundered a salute to which the Vasa fired in reply.
trans: 随后，停泊在港口的战舰们鸣响了礼炮，以示敬意；作为回应，瓦萨号（Vasa）也开炮回敬了。

name: As she emerged from her drifting cloud of gun smoke with the water churned to foam beneath her bow,
trans: 当她从那弥漫着枪炮烟雾的云层中走出来时，船头下方的水面已经泛起了层层泡沫……

name: her flags flying, pennants waving, sails filling in the breeze,
trans: 她的旗帜高高飘扬，小旗子随风摆动，船帆在微风中轻轻鼓动……

name: and the red and gold or her superstructure ablaze with colour,
trans: 那些红色和金色的装饰，以及她的上层建筑（即建筑物的主要结构），都被色彩所点亮、所照亮。

name: she presented a more majestic spectacle than Stockholmers had ever seen before.
trans: 她展现了一场比斯德哥尔摩市民前所未见的壮丽景象。

name: All gun-ports were open and the muzzles peeped wickedly from them.
trans: 所有的枪口都打开了，枪管从其中露了出来，看起来非常危险（或：极具威胁性）。

name: As the wind freshened there came a sudden squall and the ship made a strange movement, listing to port.
trans: 随着风势的增强，突然刮起了一阵狂风，船只也出现了异常的摇晃——它向左舷倾斜了过去。

name: The Ordnance officer ordered all the port cannon to be heaved to starboard
trans: 军械官命令将所有港口炮都转向右侧（即向右舷方向）。

name: to counteract the list but the steepening angle of the decks increased.
trans: 为了抵消上述问题，甲板的倾斜角度被加大了。

name: Then the sound of rumbling thunder reached the watchers on the shore,
trans: 接着，轰隆的雷声传到了岸边观望的人们耳边。

name: as cargo, ballast, ammunition and 400 people went sliding and crashing down to the port side of the steeply listing ship.
trans: 作为货物、压舱物、弹药以及400名乘客，这些物品全都沿着那艘严重倾斜的船只的船舷滑落，坠入了港口一侧的水中。

name: The lower gun-ports were now below water and the inrush sealed the ship's fate.
trans: 船上的下层炮口此时已经浸没在水中，海水涌入船内，注定了这艘船的毁灭。

name: In that first glorious hour, the mighty Vasa, which was intended to rule the Baltic,
trans: 在那个辉煌的最初时刻，那艘本应统治波罗的海的巨舰“瓦萨号”……

name: sank with all flags flying--in the harbour of her birth.
trans: 它带着所有的旗帜，在自己出生的港口沉没了。

name: Patients and doctors
trans: 患者与医生

name: What are patients looking for when they visit the doctor?
trans: 患者去看医生时，他们在寻找什么？

name: This is a sceptical age,
trans: 这是一个充满怀疑的时代。

name: but although our faith in many of the things in which our forefathers fervently believed has weakened,
trans: 这是一个充满怀疑的时代；
