name: our confidence in the curative properties of the bottle of medicine remains the same as theirs.
trans: 尽管我们对祖先们坚信的许多事物的信心已经减弱，

name: This modern faith in medicines is proved by the fact
trans: 但我们对药物疗效的信任却依然与他们一样坚定。

name: that the annual drug bill of the Health Services is mounting to astronomical figures.
trans: 这种对药物的现代信仰，从卫生服务部门的年度药品开支不断攀升（达到天文数字）这一事实中得到了证明，

name: and shows no signs at present of ceasing to rise.
trans: 而且目前这种趋势还没有停止的迹象。

name: The majority of the patients attending the medical out-patients departments of our hospitals feel that
trans: 大多数前往医院门诊部就诊的患者认为，

name: they have not received adequate treatment unless they are able to carry home with them
trans: 除非他们能带回家某种实实在在的药物作为治疗手段，

name: some tangible remedy in the shape of a bottle of medicine,
trans: 否则他们就没有得到充分的治疗。

name: a box of pills, or a small jar of ointment,
trans: 一盒药片，或者一小罐药膏。

name: and the doctor in charge of the department is only too ready to provide them with these requirements.
trans: 负责该科室的医生也非常乐意满足他们的这些要求。

name: There is no quicker method of disposing of patients than by giving them what they are asking for,
trans: 没有比满足患者的要求更快捷的“处理”他们的方法了。

name: and since most medical men in the Health Services are overworked
trans: 而且由于卫生系统中的大多数医疗人员都工作过度……

name: and have little time for offering time-consuming and little-appreciated advice on such subjects as diet,
trans: 因此，他们几乎没有时间去提供那些耗时且不太受重视的建议——比如关于饮食方面的建议。

name: right living, and the need for abandoning bad habits etc.,
trans: 正确的生活方式，以及摒弃不良习惯的必要性等等。

name: the bottle, the box, and the jar are almost always granted them.
trans: 瓶子、盒子和罐子几乎总是会给他们。

name: Nor is it only the ignorant and ill-educated person who has such faith in the bottle of medicine.
trans: 并不是只有那些无知或受教育程度低的人才会对药瓶（或药物）抱有如此大的信任（或依赖）。

name: It is recounted of Thomas Carlyle that when he heard of the illness of his friend, Henry Taylor,
trans: 据记载，当托马斯·卡莱尔得知他的朋友亨利·泰勒生病了之后……

name: he went off immediately to visit him,
trans: 他立刻动身去拜访他了。

name: carrying with him in his pocket what remained a bottle of medicine formerly prescribed for an indisposition of Mrs. Carlyle's.
trans: 他口袋里还装着剩下的一瓶药，这瓶药原本是给卡莱尔夫人开的，用于治疗她的某种疾病。

name: Carlyle was entirely ignorant of what the bottle in his pocket contained,
trans: 卡莱尔完全不知道自己口袋里的瓶子里装着什么。

name: of the nature of the illness from which his friend was suffering,
trans: 关于他的朋友所患疾病的性质……

name: and of what had previously been wrong with his wife,
trans: 以及他妻子之前存在的问题（或：他妻子之前所面临的困难/问题）。

name: but a medicine that had worked so well in one form of illness would surely be of equal benefit in another,
trans: 但是，一种在某种疾病治疗中效果非常好的药物，肯定也会对另一种疾病产生同样的治疗效果。

name: and comforted by the thought of the help he was bringing to his friend,
trans: 并且因为想到自己能为朋友提供帮助而感到欣慰（或：感到安慰）。

name: he hastened to Henry Taylor's house.
trans: 他急忙赶往亨利·泰勒的家中。

name: History does not relate whether his friend accepted his medical help, but in all probability he did.
trans: 历史并没有记载他的朋友是否接受了他的医疗帮助，但很有可能他们接受了。

name: The great advantage of taking medicine is that it makes no demands on the taker
trans: 服用药物的最大好处在于：它对服药者没有任何额外的要求（即服药者无需付出额外的努力或遵守任何特殊的规则）。

name: beyond that of putting up for a moment with a disgusting taste,
trans: 除此之外，就是暂时忍受那种令人作呕的味道罢了。

name: and that is what all patients demand of their doctors--to be cured at no inconvenience to themselves.
trans: 而这正是所有患者对医生所要求的：能够得到治疗，同时自己不必承受任何不便或麻烦。

name: The hovercraft
trans: 气垫船

name: What is a hovercraft riding on when it is in motion?
trans: 气垫船在运动时是“骑”在什么上面的呢？

name: Many strange new means of transport have been developed in our century,
trans: 在我们这个世纪，许多新型的、奇特的交通工具被开发出来了。

name: the strangest of them being perhaps the hovercraft.
trans: 其中最奇怪的，或许要数那艘气垫船了。

name: In 1953, a former electronics engineer in his fifties, Christopher Cockerell,
trans: 1953年，一位五十多岁的前电子工程师克里斯托弗·科克雷尔（Christopher Cockerell）……

name: who had turned to boat-building on the Norfolk Broads,
trans: 谁开始在诺福克河口地区从事造船业呢？

name: suggested an idea on which he had been working for many years to the British Government and industrial circles.
trans: 他向英国政府和工业界提出了一项自己多年来一直在研究的想法。

name: It was the idea of supporting a craft on a 'pad', or cushion, of low-pressure air, ringed with a curtain of higher pressure air.
trans: 这个想法的核心在于：利用一层低压空气作为“垫子”或“支撑层”来托住某个物体（比如飞行器），而该低压空气层则被一层高压空气所包围。

name: Ever since, people have had difficulty in deciding whether the craft should be ranged among ships, planes,
trans: 从那以后，人们就一直难以确定这种交通工具应该被归类为船舶、飞机中的哪一类。

name: or land vehicles--for it is something in between a boat and an aircraft.
trans: 或者陆地交通工具——因为它介于船和飞机之间。

name: As a shipbuilder, Cockerell was trying to find a solution to the problem of the wave resistance which wastes a good deal of a surface ship's power and limits its speed.
trans: 作为一名造船工程师，科克雷尔一直在努力寻找解决船舶波浪阻力问题的方法。波浪阻力会浪费船舶大量动力，并限制其航行速度。

name: His answer was to lift the vessel out of the water by making it ride on a cushion of air, no more than one or two feet thick.
trans: 他的解决方案是让船漂浮在一片空气“垫层”上，这片空气垫层的厚度不超过一两英尺。

name: This is done by a great number of ring-shaped air jets on the bottom of the craft.
trans: 这是通过飞船底部大量环形喷气装置来实现的。

name: It 'flies', therefore, but it cannot fly higher--its action depends on the surface, water or ground, over which it rides.
trans: 因此，它确实能够“飞行”，但它无法飞得更高；它的运动方式取决于它所依附的表面——无论是水面还是地面。

name: The first tests on the Solent in 1959 caused a sensation.
trans: 1959年，对“Solent”进行的初步测试引起了轰动。

name: The hovercraft travelled first over the water, then mounted the beach, climbed up the dunes, and sat down on a road.
trans: 气垫船先在水面上行驶，然后驶上了沙滩，接着爬上了沙丘，最后停在了道路上。

name: Later it crossed the Channel, riding smoothly over the waves, which presented no problem.
trans: 后来，它穿过了英吉利海峡，平稳地掠过海浪——整个过程没有任何问题。

name: Since that time, various types of hovercraft have appeared and taken up regular service.
trans: 从那时起，各种类型的气垫船相继问世，并开始被广泛使用（即投入日常运营）。

name: The hovercraft is particularly useful in large areas with poor communications such as Africa or Australia;
trans: 气垫船在通信条件较差的广大地区（如非洲或澳大利亚）特别有用。

name: it can become a 'flying fruit-bowl', carrying bananas from the plantations to the ports;
trans: 它可以变成一个“会飞的果盘”，负责将香蕉从种植园运送到港口。

name: giant hovercraft liners could span the Atlantic;
trans: 巨大的气垫船客轮或许能够横渡大西洋。

name: and the railway of the future may well be the 'hovertrain',
trans: 未来的铁路很可能会是“悬浮列车”。

name: riding on its air cushion over a single rail, which it never touches, at speeds, up to 300 m.p.h.--the possibilities appear unlimited.
trans: 这种装置依靠空气垫在单根轨道上行驶，且从未与轨道接触；其行驶速度可达到每小时300英里。由此看来，它的应用可能性似乎是无限的。

name: Exploring the sea-floor
trans: 探索海底世界

name: How did people probably imagine the sea-floor before it was investigated?
trans: 在人们开始对海底进行探索之前，他们可能是如何想象海底的样子的呢？

name: Our knowledge of the oceans a hundred years ago was confined to the two-dimensional shape of the sea surface
trans: 一百年前，我们对海洋的了解仅限于海面的二维形态。

name: and the hazards of navigation presented by the irregularities in depth of the shallow water close to the land.
trans: 以及由于靠近陆地的浅水区水深不均匀所带来的航行危险。

name: The open sea was deep and mysterious,
trans: 广阔的海洋深邃而神秘。

name: and anyone who gave more than a passing thought to the bottom confines of the oceans probably assumed that the sea-bed was flat.
trans: 任何稍微思考过海洋底部情况的人，很可能都认为海床是平坦的。

name: Sir James Clark Ross had obtained a sounding of over 2, 400 fathoms in 1839,
trans: 詹姆斯·克拉克·罗斯爵士在1839年测得水深超过了2,400英寻（约4,267米）。

name: but it was not until 1869, when H.M.S. Porcupine was put at the disposal of the Royal Society for several cruises
trans: 但直到 1869 年，“H.M.S. Porcupine”号才被交由皇家学会使用，用于多次科学考察航行。

name: that a series of deep soundings was obtained in the Atlantic and the first samples were collected by dredging the bottom.
trans: 在大西洋进行了一系列深海探测，并通过挖掘海底的方式采集到了首批样本。

name: Shortly after this the famous H.M.S. Challenger expedition established the study of the sea-floor
trans: 不久之后，著名的H.M.S.挑战者号探险队开始了对海底的研究工作。

name: as a subject worthy of the most qualified physicists and geologists.
trans: 一个值得最顶尖物理学家和地质学家研究的课题。

name: A burst of activity associated with the laying of submarine cables
trans: 与铺设海底电缆相关的一系列活动突然加剧了（即：相关活动的频率或强度突然增加了）。

name: soon confirmed the Challenger's observation that many parts of the ocean were two to three miles deep,
trans: 很快证实了挑战者的观察结果：海洋的许多区域深度在两到三英里之间。

name: and the existence of underwater features of considerable magnitude.
trans: 以及水下存在一些规模相当大的地质结构（或地貌特征）。

name: Today, enough soundings are available to enable a relief map of the Atlantic to be drawn
trans: 如今，我们已经收集到了足够多的数据，可以绘制出大西洋的海底地形图（即“海底 relief map”）。

name: and we know something of the great variety of the sea bed's topography.
trans: 我们对海底地形的多样性也有所了解。

name: Since the sea covers the greater part of the earth's surface,
trans: 由于海洋覆盖了地球表面的大部分区域，

name: it is quite reasonable to regard the sea floor as the basic form of the crust of the earth,
trans: 将海底视为地球地壳的基本构成部分，这是完全合理的。

name: with superimposed upon it the continents,
trans: 在这些图像上，大陆的轮廓被叠加显示了出来。

name: together with the islands and other features of the oceans.
trans: 连同海洋中的岛屿以及其他地形特征一起。

name: The continents form rugged tablelands which stand nearly three miles above the floor of the open ocean.
trans: 这些大陆形成了崎岖的高原地带，其海拔高度几乎达到了开放海域底部的三英里（约4.8公里）。

name: From the shore line, out to a distance which may be anywhere from a few miles to a few hundred miles,
trans: 从海岸线开始，延伸到距离海岸几英里到几百英里的范围内……

name: runs the gentle slope of the continental shelf, geologically part of the continents.
trans: 沿着大陆架的平缓坡度延伸；从地质学角度来看，大陆架属于大陆的一部分。

name: The real dividing line between continents and oceans occurs at the foot of a steeper slope.
trans: 实际上，大陆与海洋之间的分界线位于一个更陡峭的斜坡的底部。

name: This continental slope usually starts at a place somewhere near the 100-fathom mark
trans: 这个大陆坡通常始于水深约100英寻（约30米）的位置。

name: and in the course of a few hundred miles reaches the true ocean floor at 2, 500-3, 500 fathoms.
trans: 在行驶了数百英里的过程中，它最终抵达了真正的海底，那里的海底深度为2,500至3,500英寻（约762至1,067米）。

name: The slope averages about 1 in 30, but contains steep,
trans: 坡度的平均比例约为 1:30（即每下降 30 单位距离，高度仅下降 1 单位距离），不过其中也包含一些非常陡峭的部分。

name: probably vertical, cliffs, and gentle sediment-covered terraces,
trans: 可能是垂直的悬崖，以及被松软沉积物覆盖的缓坡地形。

name: and near its lower reaches there is a long tailing-off which is almost certainly the result of
trans: 在其下游附近，有一条逐渐变缓的河道（或水流区域）；这几乎可以肯定是某种自然现象或人为活动的结果。

name: material transported out to deep water after being eroded from the continental masses.
trans: 这些物质是从大陆上被侵蚀后，被输送到深水区的。

name: The sculptor speaks
trans: 雕塑家开口说话了。

name: What do you have to be able to do to appreciate sculpture?
trans: 要真正欣赏雕塑，你需要具备哪些条件或能力呢？

name: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in 3 dimensions.
trans: 对雕塑的欣赏，取决于人们能否理解和回应三维空间中的形态（即雕塑的立体结构与形态特征）。

name: That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts;
trans: 也许正因为如此，雕塑才被人们称为所有艺术形式中最难掌握的一种。

name: certainly it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
trans: 当然，这比那些只需要欣赏二维平面形状的艺术形式要困难得多。

name: Many more people are 'form-blind' than colour-blind.
trans: 实际上，有更多的人存在“形式盲”（即无法区分不同形式的视觉信息）的问题，而不是“色盲”（即无法区分不同颜色的视觉信息）。

name: The child learning to see, first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape; it cannot judge distances, depths.
trans: 正在学习视力的孩子最初只能识别二维的形状；他们还无法判断距离或物体的深度。

name: Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop (partly by means of touch) the ability to judge roughly 3-dimensonal distances.
trans: 后来，为了自身的安全以及实际生活的需要，它必须逐渐培养出判断三维空间距离的能力（这部分是通过触觉来实现的）。

name: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
trans: 然而，在满足了实际需求之后，大多数人就不会再进一步去追求更高的目标了。

name: Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form,
trans: 尽管它们在识别平面图形方面可以达到相当高的准确度，

name: they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
trans: 他们没有付出进一步的智力与情感努力，去全面理解“形式”在其空间存在中的本质（即形式在三维空间中的具体表现方式）。

name: This is what the sculptor must do.
trans: 这就是雕塑家必须做的事情。

name: He must strive continually to think of and use, form in its full spatial completeness.
trans: 他必须不断努力，去思考并运用那些能够完整地反映空间结构的概念（或方法）。

name: He gets the solid shape as it were, inside his head--he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.
trans: 他在脑海中清晰地想象出那个物体的形状；无论这个物体的实际大小如何，他都仿佛能够将其完全握在手中一样。

name: He mentally visualizes a complex form from all round itself;
trans: 他在脑海中想象出一个从各个方向看都呈复杂形状的物体（或结构）。

name: he knows while he looks at one side what the other side is like; he identifies himself with its centre of gravity, its mass, its weight;
trans: 当他注视着某一方时，他其实也知道另一方的样子；他将自己与那方的“重心”、“质量”以及“重量”联系在一起（即将自己视为那方的一个组成部分）。

name: he realizes its volume as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
trans: 他认识到这个物体的“体积”，其实就是该物体在空气中占据的空间（即该物体将空气“挤开”后所形成的空间）。

name: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
trans: 对于雕塑而言，敏锐的观察者也必须学会纯粹地将形状视为形状本身来感知它，而不是将其视为某种描述或回忆的象征。

name: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape quite apart from its significance as food,
trans: 例如，他必须将鸡蛋仅仅视为一个简单的、独立的固体形状，而忽略其作为食物的意义。

name: or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
trans: 或者，基于这种文学观念——即它最终会变成一只鸟。

name: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom,
trans: 因此，对于像贝壳、螺母、李子、梨子、蝌蚪、蘑菇这样的固体物体来说……

name: a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree-trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
trans: 一座山峰、一个肾脏、一根胡萝卜、一根树干、一只鸟、一个花蕾、一只云雀、一只瓢虫、一种香蒲植物、一根骨头。

name: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.
trans: 从这些基础形式出发，他可以进一步理解更复杂的结构，或是几种形式之间的组合。

name: Galileo reborn
trans: 伽利略的重生

name: What has modified our traditional view of Galileo in recent times?
trans: 是什么在最近改变了我们对伽利略的传统看法？

name: In his own lifetime Galileo was the centre of violent controversy, but the scientific dust has long since settled,
trans: 在伽利略有生之年，他一直是激烈争议的焦点；然而，那些科学上的争论早已平息，尘埃也已落定。

name: and today we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
trans: 今天，我们终于能够以更加客观的角度来看待他那场著名的与宗教裁判所的冲突了。

name: But, in contrast, it is only in modern times that Galileo has become a problem child for historians of science.
trans: 然而，恰恰相反，直到现代，伽利略才成为科学史学家们争论的焦点（或者说，伽利略才被视作一个“麻烦人物”）。

name: The old view of Galileo was delightfully uncomplicated.
trans: 人们对伽利略的看法过去非常简单明了（即：人们过去对伽利略的看法非常直接、容易理解）。

name: He was, above all, a man who experimented:
trans: 他首先是一个喜欢进行实验的人。

name: who despised the prejudice and book learning of the Aristotelians,
trans: 那些鄙视亚里士多德学派偏见以及他们对书本知识的过度依赖的人……

name: who put his questions to nature instead of to the ancients, and who drew his conclusions fearlessly.
trans: 那些将自己的疑问投向大自然（而非古人），并勇敢地得出自己结论的人，才是真正的探索者。

name: He had been the first to turn a telescope to the sky,
trans: 他是第一个将望远镜对准天空的人。

name: and he had seen there evidence enough to overthrow Aristotle and Ptolemy together.
trans: 他看到了足够的证据，足以推翻亚里士多德和托勒密的理论。

name: He was the man who climbed the Leaning Tower of Pisa and dropped various weights from the top,
trans: 他就是那个爬上比萨斜塔并从塔顶扔下各种重物的人。

name: who rolled balls down inclined planes, and then generalized the results of his many experiments into the famous law of free fall.
trans: 是谁让球从斜面上滚下来，然后将他的大量实验结果归纳成了著名的自由落体定律呢？

name: But a closer study of the evidence,
trans: 但是，对证据进行更仔细的研究之后……

name: supported by a deeper sense of the period, and particularly by a new consciousness of the philosophical undercurrents in the scientific revolution,
trans: 这种理解基于对那个时代背景的更深刻认识，尤其是对科学革命中潜藏的哲学思潮的新颖洞察。

name: has profoundly modified this view of Galileo.
trans: 这极大地改变了人们对伽利略的看法。

name: Today, although the old Galileo lives on in many popular writings, among historians of science a new and more sophisticated picture has emerged.
trans: 如今，尽管老伽利略的形象仍然存在于许多通俗的文学作品中，但在科学史学家们看来，关于他的新观点和更复杂的认识已经逐渐形成。

name: At the same time our sympathy for Galileo's opponents has grown somewhat.
trans: 与此同时，我们对伽利略的反对者的同情心也有所增加。

name: His telescopic observations are justly immortal;
trans: 他的望远镜观测成果当之无愧地被载入史册，永垂不朽。

name: they aroused great interest at the time,
trans: 它们在当时引起了极大的兴趣。

name: they had important theoretical consequences,
trans: 这些理论具有重要的意义（或：这些理论产生了重要的影响/后果）。

name: and they provided a striking demonstration of the potentialities hidden in instruments and apparatus.
trans: 他们展示了一个令人印象深刻的例子，证明了各种仪器和设备所隐藏的巨大潜力。

name: But can we blame those who looked and failed to see what Galileo saw,
trans: 但是，我们能责怪那些明明有机会却未能看到伽利略所发现的东西的人吗？

name: if we remember that to use a telescope at the limit of its powers calls for long experience and intimate familiarity with one's instrument?
trans: 如果我们记得：要使用一台性能已达到极限的望远镜，就需要具备丰富的使用经验，并且对这台仪器有非常深入的了解（即对其工作原理、操作方法等了如指掌）的话……

name: Was the philosopher who refused to look through Galileo's telescope more culpable than those who alleged
trans: 那位拒绝通过伽利略的望远镜观察天体的哲学家，是否比那些指责伽利略的人更应该受到责备呢？

name: that the spiral nebulae observed with Lord Rosse's great telescope in the 1840s were scratches left by the grinder?
trans: 那些在19世纪40年代由罗斯勋爵使用他的大型望远镜观测到的螺旋星云，其实只是研磨机留下的痕迹罢了？

name: We can perhaps forgive those who said the moons of Jupiter were produced by Galileo's spyglass if we recall that in his day,
trans: 或许我们可以原谅那些认为木星的卫星是由伽利略用望远镜观测到的的人。毕竟，在他那个时代，望远镜还处于刚刚被发明、技术还不成熟的状态。

name: as for centuries before, curved glass was the popular contrivance for producing not truth but illusion, untruth;
trans: 与几个世纪前的情况一样，曲面玻璃当时被广泛用于制造的不是“真相”，而是“幻觉”——即虚假的表象。

name: and if a single curved glass would distort nature, how much more would a pair of them?
trans: 如果一块弯曲的玻璃都会扭曲自然界的景象，那么两块弯曲的玻璃又会产生多大的扭曲效果呢？

name: Education
trans: 教育

name: Why is education democratic in bookless tribal societies?
trans: 为什么在那些没有书籍的部落社会中，教育仍然是民主的（即教育过程体现了平等与参与的原则）？

name: Education is one of the key words of our time.
trans: “教育”是我们这个时代的核心关键词之一。

name: A man without an education, many of us believe,
trans: 我们中的许多人认为，一个没有受过教育的人……

name: is an unfortunate victim of adverse circumstances, deprived of one of the greatest twentieth-century opportunities.
trans: 他只是不幸的受害者，被恶劣的环境所剥夺了二十世纪最伟大的机遇之一。

name: Convinced of the importance of education, modern states 'invest' in institutions of learning to get back 'interest'
trans: 意识到教育的重要性，现代国家会投资于各类教育机构，以期从中获得回报（即实现教育投资带来的社会效益或经济效益）。

name: in the form of a large group of enlightened young men and women who are potential leaders.
trans: 以一群富有智慧、充满理想的年轻人为核心；这些年轻人都是未来的潜在领导者。

name: Education, with its cycles of instruction so carefully worked out,
trans: 教育，其教学流程都是经过精心设计的……

name: punctuated by textbooks--those purchasable wells of wisdom--what would civilization be like without its benefits?
trans: 如果文明失去了那些可以购买的、充满智慧的教科书，它会变成什么样子呢？

name: So much is certain: that we would have doctors and preachers,
trans: 有几点是确定的：我们一定会拥有医生和传教士。

name: lawyers and defendants marriages and births--but our spiritual outlook would be different.
trans: 律师、被告、婚姻、出生……但这些因素并不会改变我们的精神面貌（即我们的价值观或人生观）。

name: We would lay less stress on 'facts and figures' and more on a good memory,
trans: 我们会减少对“事实和数据”的依赖，而更加重视良好的记忆力。

name: on applied psychology, and on the capacity of a man to get along with his fellow-citizens.
trans: 应用心理学，以及一个人与同胞相处、共处的可能性（或：一个人适应社会、与他人建立良好关系的能力）。

name: If our educational system were fashioned after its bookless past we would have the most democratic form of 'college' imaginable.
trans: 如果我们的教育体系能够借鉴其过去“无书籍”的教育模式，那么我们将会拥有迄今为止最民主形式的“大学”。

name: Among tribal people all knowledge inherited by tradition is shared by all;
trans: 在部落社会中，所有通过传统传承下来的知识都是大家共同拥有的。

name: it is taught to every member of the tribe so that in this respect everybody is equally equipped for life.
trans: 这个知识被传授给部落的每一个成员，这样在这一点上，每个人都能为生活做好充分的准备，具备相同的生存能力。

name: It is the ideal condition of the 'equal start' which only our most progressive forms of modern education try to regain.
trans: 这正是“公平竞争起点”这一理想状态的体现；只有我们现代教育中最先进、最具前瞻性的教育体系，才试图重新实现这一状态。

name: In primitive cultures the obligation to seek and to receive the traditional instruction is binding to all.
trans: 在原始文化中，寻求并接受传统教诲的义务对所有人都是具有约束力的。

name: There are no'illiterates' --if the term can be applied to peoples without a script--while our own compulsory school attendance became law in Germany in 1642,
trans: 其实并不存在所谓的“文盲”——如果“文盲”这个词指的是那些不识字的人的话。在德国，强制性的义务教育制度直到 1642 年才被立法成为法律。

name: in France in 1806, and in England in 1876 and is still nonexistent in a number of 'civilized' nations.
trans: 这一制度最早出现在1806年的法国，以及1876年的英国；然而，在许多“文明国家”中，它至今仍然不存在。

name: This shows how long it was before we deemed it necessary to make sure
trans: 这表明了我们花了多长时间才认为有必要采取行动（或：这显示了在我们认为有必要采取行动之前，已经过去了多长时间）。

name: that all our children could share in the knowledge accumulated by the 'happy few' during the past centuries.
trans: 这样，我们所有的孩子都能享受到过去几个世纪里那些“幸运的少数人”所积累的知识。

name: Education in the wilderness is not a matter of monetary means.
trans: 在偏远地区提供教育，并不是取决于资金多少的问题。

name: All are entitled to an equal start.
trans: 每个人都应该拥有平等的起点。

name: There is none of the hurry which, in our society, often hampers the full development of a growing personality.
trans: 在我们的社会中，往往存在着一种急躁的情绪，这种情绪会阻碍个人成长与自我发展的过程。

name: There, a child grows up under the everpresent attention of his parents;
trans: 在那里，一个孩子在父母无时无刻不在的关注下长大。

name: therefore the jungles and the savannahs know of no 'juvenile delinquency'.
trans: 因此，丛林和草原地区根本不存在“青少年犯罪”这种现象。

name: No necessity of making a living away from home results in neglect of children, and no father is confronted with his inability to 'buy' an education for his child.
trans: 如果没有必要离家去谋生，就可能导致对孩子的忽视；而没有任何父亲会因为自己无力为孩子提供教育而感到无能为力（即没有父亲会因为经济原因而无法让孩子接受教育）。

name: Adolescence
trans: 青春期

name: What do adolescents respect in parents?
trans: 青少年在父母身上尊重什么？

name: Parents are often upset when their children praise the homes of their friends and regard it as a slur on their own cooking, or cleaning, or furniture,
trans: 当孩子们夸赞朋友家的环境时，父母往往会感到不满，他们认为这种行为是对自己烹饪水平、清洁工作或家具质量的贬低。

name: and often are foolish enough to let the adolescents see that they are annoyed.
trans: 他们常常犯愚蠢的错误，让青少年察觉到他们其实很恼火（或：他们总是犯傻，以至于让青少年看出来他们很生气）。

name: They may even accuse them of disloyalty, or make some spiteful remark about the friends' parents.
trans: 他们甚至可能会指责这些人不忠，或者对这些人朋友的父母说一些刻薄的话。

name: Such a loss of dignity and descent into childish behaviour on the part of the adults deeply shocks the adolescents,
trans: 成年人这种丧失尊严、行为变得幼稚的现象，令青少年们感到极为震惊。

name: and makes them resolve that in future they will not talk to their parents about the places or people they visit.
trans: 这让他们决定：以后不会再和父母谈论自己去过的地方或遇到的人。

name: Before very long the parents will be complaining that the child is so secretive and never tells them anything,
trans: 用不了多久，父母们就会开始抱怨孩子太保密了，从不跟他们透露任何事情。

name: but they seldom realize that they have brought this on themselves.
trans: 但他们很少意识到，这一切其实都是他们自己造成的。

name: Disillusionment with the parents,
trans: 对父母的失望（或：对父母的失望情绪）

name: however good and adequate they may be both as parents and as individuals, is to some degree inevitable.
trans: 无论他们作为父母或作为个体有多么优秀和称职，这种（某种情况）在某种程度上都是不可避免的。

name: Most children have such a high ideal of their parents,
trans: 大多数孩子对他们的父母都有着非常高的期望（或：对父母有着非常美好的想象）。

name: unless the parents themselves have been unsatisfactory, that it can hardly hope to stand up to a realistic evaluation.
trans: 除非父母本身的表现令人不满意，否则这样的教育方式很难经得起现实的评估。

name: Parents would be greatly surprised and deeply touched if they realized how much belief their children usually have in their character and infallibility,
trans: 如果父母意识到他们的孩子通常对自己的人格以及他们的“绝对正确性”抱有多大的信任，他们一定会感到非常惊讶和深受感动。

name: and how much this faith means to a child.
trans: 以及这种信念对一个孩子来说意味着什么。

name: If parents were prepared for this adolescent reaction,
trans: 如果父母能够预料到青少年会有这样的反应……

name: and realized that was a sign that the child was growing up
trans: 我意识到，这正是孩子正在成长的一个迹象。

name: and developing valuable powers of observation and independent judgment,
trans: 同时培养出宝贵的观察能力和独立判断力。

name: they would not be so hurt, and therefore would not drive the child into opposition by resenting and resisting it.
trans: 他们就不会受到那么大的伤害；因此，也不会因为感到怨恨和抗拒而让孩子与他们产生对立情绪。

name: The adolescent, with his passion for sincerity,
trans: 这个青少年，对真诚充满热情……

name: always respects a parent who admits that he is wrong, or ignorant,
trans: 总是尊重那些承认自己犯错或自己无知的人的父母。

name: or even that he has been unfair or unjust.
trans: 或者甚至认为他行为不公平或不公正。

name: What the child cannot forgive is the parents' refusal to admit these charges if the child knows them to be true.
trans: 孩子无法原谅的是：即使孩子知道这些指控是真实的，父母却拒绝承认它们。

name: Victorian parents believed that they kept their dignity by retreating behind an unreasoning authoritarian attitude in fact they did nothing of the kind,
trans: 维多利亚时代的父母认为，通过采取一种不合理的、专制的态度来维护自己的尊严；但实际上，他们根本并没有这样做。

name: but children were then too cowed to let them know how they really felt.
trans: 但那时孩子们都太胆小了，不敢说出自己的真实感受。

name: Today we tend to go to the other extreme,
trans: 如今，我们往往走向另一个极端。

name: but on the whole this is a healthier attitude both for the child and the parent.
trans: 但总体来说，这种态度对孩子的成长以及父母的心理状态都有益处（即更健康）。

name: It is always wiser and safer to face up to reality, however painful it may be at the moment.
trans: 无论此刻的现实有多么痛苦，直面现实总是更为明智、也更安全的选择。

name: Space odyssey
trans: 《太空漫游》

name: When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonising Mars?
trans: 我们什么时候才能真正认真地考虑在火星上建立殖民地呢？

name: The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System supplying the rocket fuels for its ships,
trans: 月球很可能会成为太阳系的工业中心，为宇宙飞船提供所需的火箭燃料。

name: easily obtainable from the lunar rocks in the form of liquid oxygen.
trans: 这种物质可以从月球岩石中轻易提取出来，其形式为液态氧。

name: The reason lies in its gravity.
trans: 原因在于它的重力。

name: Because the Moon has only an eightieth of the Earth's mass,
trans: 因为月球的质量只有地球的八十分之一，

name: it requires 97% less energy
trans: 它所需的能量减少了 97%。

name: to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon to Earth-orbit than the 200 mile-journey from Earth's surface into orbit!
trans: 从月球到地球的轨道距离长达二十五万英里，这比从地球表面发射卫星进入地球轨道所需的二百英里旅程要长得多！

name: This may sound fantastic, but it is easily calculated.
trans: 这听起来可能很棒，但实际上这个数值是可以很容易地计算出来的。

name: To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must travel at seven miles per second.
trans: 要乘坐火箭逃离地球，必须以每秒七英里的速度飞行。

name: The comparable speed from the Moon is only 1.5 miles per second.
trans: 从月球上看，物体的相对速度仅为每秒1.5英里。

name: Because the gravity on the Moon's surface is only a sixth of Earth's (remember how easily the Apollo astronauts bounded along),
trans: 因为月球表面的重力只有地球的六分之一（还记得阿波罗宇航员在月球上行走时是多么轻松自如吗？）

name: it takes much less energy to accelerate to that 1.5mps than it does on Earth.
trans: 在月球上，将物体加速到 1.5 米每秒所需的能量要比在地球上少得多。

name: Moon dwellers will be able to fly in space at only three percent of the cost of similar journeys by their terrestrial cousins.
trans: 月球居民在太空中旅行的费用，将仅为地球上的宇航员进行类似旅程所需费用的3%。

name: Arthur C.Clark once suggested a revolutionary idea passes through three phases:
trans: 阿瑟·C·克拉克曾提出一个观点：一个革命性的想法通常会经历三个阶段：

name: 1.  'It's impossible--don't waste my time.'
trans: “这不可能——别浪费我的时间了。”

name: 2.  'It's possible, but not worth doing.'
trans: 2. “这是可能的，但并不值得去做。”

name: 3.  'I said it was a good idea all along.'
trans: 3. “我一直都说这是个好主意。”

name: The idea of colonising Mars--a world 160 times more distant than the Moon--will move decisively from the second phase to the third,
trans: 将火星（一个距离地球比月球远160倍的天体）殖民化的计划，将正式从第二阶段进入第三阶段。

name: when a significant number of people are living permanently in space.
trans: 当有相当数量的人能够在太空中永久居住时……

name: Mars has an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers.
trans: 火星对那些渴望踏上太空之旅的人来说，具有难以抗拒的吸引力。

name: America, Russia and Europe are filled with enthusiasts--many of them serious and senior scientists who dream of sending people to it.
trans: 美国、俄罗斯和欧洲都充满了热衷于这项事业的人；其中许多人都是经验丰富的科学家，他们梦想着能够将人类送往那里（即实现人类探索该目标）。

name: Their aim is understandable.
trans: 他们的目标是可以理解的。

name: It is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth.
trans: 它是太阳系中与地球最为相似的行星。

name: It is a world of red sandy deserts (hence its name--the Red Planet),
trans: 这是一个遍布红色沙质沙漠的世界（因此它被称为“红色星球”）。

name: cloudless skies, savage sandstorms, chasms wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest.
trans: 万里无云的天空、猛烈的沙尘暴、比大峡谷还要宽阔的峡谷，以及至少有一座比珠穆朗玛峰高出两倍以上的山峰。

name: It seems ideal for settlement.
trans: 这似乎非常适合用于定居。

name: The cost of government
trans: 政府的开支（或成本）

name: What's the most important factor, both in government or business, for keeping running costs low?
trans: 在政府或企业中，保持运营成本处于较低水平的最重要因素是什么？

name: If a nation is essentialy disunited, it is left to the government to hold it together.
trans: 如果一个国家本质上处于分裂状态，那么维持国家的统一就只能依靠政府的力量了。

name: This increases the expense of government, and reduces correspondingly the amount of economic resources that could be used for developing the country.
trans: 这增加了政府的开支，相应地减少了可用于国家发展的经济资源。

name: And it should not be forgotten how small those resources are in a poor and backward country.
trans: 而且我们不应忘记：在这样一个贫穷且落后的国家里，这些资源是多么的匮乏（或者说，这些资源的数量是多么的有限）。

name: Where the cost of government is high, resources for development are correspondingly low.
trans: 在政府开支较高的地方，用于发展的资源相应地也会减少。

name: This may be illustrated by comparing the position of a nation with that of a private business enterprise.
trans: 这可以通过将一个国家的地位与一家私营企业的地位进行比较来说明。

name: An enterprise has to incur certain costs and expenses in order to stay in business.
trans: 企业必须承担一定的成本和开支，才能维持自身的运营。

name: For our purposes, we are concerned only with one kind of cost--the cost of managing and administering the business.
trans: 就我们的目的而言，我们只关注一种成本——即管理和运营企业的成本。

name: Such administrative overheads in a business are analogous to the cost of government in a nation.
trans: 在企业中，这些行政开销就相当于一个国家中的政府开支。

name: The administrative overheads of a business are low to the extent that everyone working in the business
trans: 该企业的行政开支非常低，以至于企业里的每一位员工都能从中受益（即：行政成本如此之低，以至于不会给员工的工作带来任何负担或负面影响）。

name: can be trusted to behave in a way that best promotes the interests of the firm.
trans: 可以信赖他们会以最有利于公司利益的方式行事。

name: If they can each be trusted to take such responsibilities,
trans: 如果他们每个人都能被信任去承担这样的责任的话……

name: and to exercise such initiative as falls within their sphere, then administrative overheads will be low.
trans: 如果他们能够在自己的职责范围内主动采取行动，那么行政成本将会很低。

name: It will be low because it will be necessary to have only one man looking after each job without having another man to check upon what he is doing,
trans: 这个数字会很低，因为每项工作只需要由一个人来负责，而不需要另一个人去监督他的工作进度。

name: keep him in line, and report on him to someone else.
trans: 让他遵守规定，并向其他人汇报他的表现。

name: But if no one can be trusted to act in a loyal and responsible manner towards his job,
trans: 但如果没有人能够被信任以忠诚和负责任的态度对待自己的工作的话……

name: then the business will require armies of administrators, checkers and foremen and administrative overheads will rise correspondingly.
trans: 那么，企业将需要大量的管理人员、审核人员以及工头；相应的，管理成本也会随之增加。

name: As administrative overheads rise, so the earnings of the business after meeting the expense of administration, will fall;
trans: 随着行政开支的增加，企业在扣除行政费用后的净利润也会相应下降。

name: and the business will have less money to distribute as dividends or invest directly in its future progress and development.
trans: 这样一来，企业可用于分配作为股息的资金，以及用于直接投资其未来发展与进步的资金，都会减少。

name: It is precisely the same with a nation.
trans: 对于一个国家来说，情况也是如此。

name: To the extent that the people can be relied on to behave in a loyal and responsible manner,
trans: 在人们能够被信赖、会以忠诚和负责任的方式行事的前提下，

name: the government does not require armies of police and civil servants to keep them in order.
trans: 政府并不需要大量的警察和公务员来维持社会秩序。

name: But if a nation is disunited, the government cannot be sure that the actions of the people will be in the interests of the nation;
trans: 但是，如果一个国家处于分裂状态，政府就无法确保人民的行为会符合国家的利益。

name: and it will have to watch, check, and control the people accordingly.
trans: 它将不得不监视这些人，对他们进行评估，并据此采取相应的控制措施。

name: A disunited nation therefore has to incur unduly high costs of government.
trans: 因此，一个分裂的国家不得不承担过高额的政府开支。

name: The process of ageing
trans: 衰老的过程

name: What is one of the most unpleasant discoveries we make about ourselves as we get older?
trans: 随着年龄的增长，关于我们自己，我们会发现哪些最令人不快的真相（或事实）呢？

name: At the age of twelve years, the human body is at its most vigorous.
trans: 在十二岁的时候，人体正处于最旺盛的发育阶段。

name: It has yet to reach its full size and strength, and its owner his or her full intelligence: but at this age the likelihood of death is least.
trans: 它还没有达到自己的最大体型和最强壮的状态，其主人也尚未发挥出全部智力；不过在这个阶段，死亡的风险是最小的。

name: Earlier, we were infants and young children, and consequently more vulnerable;
trans: 早些时候，我们还是婴儿和幼儿，因此更加脆弱。

name: later, we shall undergo a progressive loss of our vigour and resistance which, though imperceptible at first
trans: 后来，我们的体力和抵抗力会逐渐减弱；虽然这种变化起初并不明显，但最终会变得显而易见。

name: will finally become so steep that we can live no longer,
trans: 最终，情况会变得如此糟糕（或：形势会变得如此严峻），以至于我们再也无法生存下去了。

name: however well we look after ourselves, and however well society, and our doctors, look after us.
trans: 无论我们自己多么注重保养身体，无论社会和医生为我们提供了多么优质的医疗服务，情况依然可能不尽如人意。

name: This decline in vigour with the passing of time is called ageing.
trans: 这种随着时间推移而逐渐减弱的能力或活力，被称为“衰老”。

name: It is one of the most unpleasant discoveries which we all make that we must decline in this way, that if we escape wars,
trans: 这是我们所有人都会遇到的最令人不快的发现之一：我们必须以这种方式拒绝某些事情（或选择放弃某些机会）。即使我们成功避开了战争，依然无法逃避这种无奈的现实。

name: accidents and diseases we shall eventually 'die of old age', and that this happens at a rate which differs little from person to person,
trans: 无论是意外事故还是疾病，我们最终都会“因年老而死亡”，而且这种死亡的发生率在人与人之间几乎没有差异。

name: so that there are heavy odds in favour of our dying between the ages of 65 and 80.
trans: 因此，我们在 65 到 80 岁之间死亡的概率非常高。

name: Some of us will die sooner, a few will live longer -- on into a ninth or tenth decade.
trans: 我们中的一些人会早逝，而另一些人则会活得更长，甚至能活到九十多岁或一百岁。

name: But the chances are against it,
trans: 但是，这种可能性非常小（或者说，成功的几率很低）。

name: and there is a virtual limit on how long we can hope to remain alive, however lucky and robust we are.
trans: 无论我们多么幸运、身体多么强健，我们的生命都存在一个客观的、无法超越的极限。

name: Normal people tend to forget this process unless and until they are reminded of it.
trans: 普通人往往会忘记这个过程，除非有人提醒他们。

name: We are so familiar with the fact that man ages, that people have for years assumed that the process of losing vigour with time,
trans: 我们非常清楚人类会衰老这一事实；多年来，人们一直认为随着时间的推移，人体会逐渐失去活力（即身体机能会逐渐衰退）。

name: of becoming more likely to die the older we get, was something self-evident
trans: 随着年龄的增长，死亡风险增加这一事实是显而易见的。

name: like the cooling of a hot kettle or the wearing-out of a pair of shoes.
trans: 就像热水壶冷却下来，或者一双鞋子被穿破一样。

name: They have also assumed that all animals,
trans: 他们还假设所有的动物……

name: and probably other organisms such as trees, or even the universe itself, must in the nature of things 'wear out'.
trans: 很可能其他生物（比如树木），甚至整个宇宙本身，按照自然规律也都会“逐渐磨损”或衰败。

name: Most animals we commonly observe do in fact age as we do,
trans: 我们日常生活中观察到的大多数动物确实会像我们一样衰老。

name: if given the chance to live long enough;
trans: 如果有机会活得足够长的话……

name: and mechanical systems like a wound watch, or the sun,
trans: 以及像有故障的手表或太阳这样的机械系统。

name: do in fact run out of energy in accordance with the second law of thermodynamics (whether the whole universe does so is a moot point at present).
trans: 根据热力学第二定律，能量确实会逐渐耗尽（不过整个宇宙是否会最终耗尽能量，目前仍是一个有争议的问题）。

name: But these are not analogous to what happens when man ages.
trans: 但这些情况与人类衰老过程中的变化并不相似。

name: A run-down watch is still a watch and can be rewound.
trans: 一块虽然已经损坏（或功能失调）的手表仍然是一块手表，而且可以重新上发条（使其继续运行）。

name: An old watch, by contrast, becomes so worn and unreliable that it eventually is not worth mending.
trans: 相比之下，一块旧手表会因为长时间的使用而变得非常破旧、不可靠，最终甚至不值得修理了。

name: But a watch could never repair itself--it does not consist of living parts, only of metal, which wears away by friction.
trans: 但是，手表永远无法自我修复——它并没有任何“活的”部件，只由金属构成，而金属会因摩擦而逐渐磨损。

name: We could, at one time, repair ourselves--well enough, at least, to overcome all but the most instantly fatal illnesses and accidents.
trans: 曾经，我们能够自我修复——至少能够修复到足以克服除那些瞬间致命的疾病和意外之外的所有伤害的程度。

name: Between twelve and eighty years we gradually lose this power;
trans: 在十二岁到八十岁之间，我们逐渐失去了这种能力（或：在人生的这个阶段，我们逐渐丧失了某种特定的能力）。

name: an illness which at 12 would knock us over, at 80 can knock us out, and into our grave.
trans: 一种疾病：在12岁时就可能让我们倒下（失去健康），而在80岁时则可能让我们彻底失去生命，直接送我们进坟墓。

name: If we could stay as vigorous as we are at twelve,
trans: 如果我们能保持十二岁时那样的活力和精力……

name: it would take about 700 years for half of us to die, and another 700 for the survivors to be reduced by half again.
trans: 大约需要700年的时间，我们中的一半人会死去；再过700年，剩下的幸存者数量又会减少一半。

name: Water and the traveller
trans: 水与旅行者

name: What does this text describe?
trans: 这段文字描述了什么？

name: Contamination of water supplies is usually due to poor sanitation close to water sources,
trans: 水源的污染通常是由于水源附近卫生条件差所导致的。

name: sewage disposal into the sources themselves, leakage of sewage into distribution systems or contamination with industrial or farm waste.
trans: 污水被直接排放到水源中；污水泄漏到供水系统中；或者水源被工业或农业废弃物污染。

name: Even if a piped water supply is safe at its source, it is not always safe by the time it reaches the tap.
trans: 即使管道输送的自来水在源头是安全的，但在到达水龙头时也不一定还是安全的。

name: Intermittent tap-water supplies should be regarded as particularly suspect.
trans: 间歇性的自来水供应情况应该被视为非常可疑的（即可能存在问题或安全隐患）。

name: Travellers on short trips to areas with water supplies of uncertain quality
trans: 前往水质不稳定的地区的短途旅行者

name: should avoid drinking tap-water, or untreated water from any other source.
trans: 应避免饮用自来水或来自其他任何来源的未经处理的水。

name: It is best to keep to hot drinks, bottled or canned drinks of well-known brand names-international standard of water treatment are usually followed at bottling plants.
trans: 最好选择热饮，或者选择知名品牌生产的瓶装或罐装饮料。这些饮料的生产工厂通常采用国际标准的水处理工艺。

name: Carbonated drinks are acidic, and slightly safer.
trans: 碳酸饮料呈酸性，相对来说比较“安全”（即对健康的影响较小）。

name: Make sure that all bottles are opened in your presence, and that their rims are clean and dry.
trans: 请确保所有瓶子都在你的监督下被打开，并且瓶口的边缘保持干净、干燥的状态。

name: Boiling is always a good way of treating water.
trans: 煮沸始终是处理水的一种有效方法。

name: Some hotels supply boiled water on request and this can be used for drinking, or for brushing teeth.
trans: 有些酒店会根据客人的要求提供煮沸的水，这种水可以用来饮用或刷牙。

name: Portable boiling elements that can boil small quantities of water are useful when the right voltage of electricity is available.
trans: 便携式煮水装置在能够提供合适电压的电力条件下非常实用，因为它们可以用来烧开少量的水。

name: Refuse politely any cold drink from an unknown source.
trans: 礼貌地拒绝任何来自陌生人的冷饮。

name: Ice is only as safe as the water from which it is made,
trans: 冰的安全性取决于构成它的水的质量。

name: and should not be put in drinks unless it is known to be safe.
trans: 除非确定它是安全的，否则不应该将其添加到饮料中。

name: Drinks can be cooled by placing them on ice rather than adding ice to them.
trans: 饮料可以通过将其放在冰块上来冷却，而不是在饮料中加入冰块。

name: Alcohol may be a medical disinfectant, but should not be relied upon to sterilize water.
trans: 酒精虽然可以用作医疗消毒剂，但不应依赖它来对水进行杀菌处理。

name: Ethanol is more effective at a concentration of 50-70 percent;
trans: 乙醇在浓度为50%至70%时效果更佳。

name: below 20 per cent, its bactericidal action is negligible.
trans: 当其浓度低于20%时，其杀菌效果几乎可以忽略不计。

name: Spirits labelled 95 proof contain only about 47 per cent alcohol.
trans: 标有“95度”酒精含量的酒类，实际上只含有大约47%的酒精。

name: Beware of methylated alcohol,
trans: 请注意：甲醇（methylated alcohol）是一种危险的物质，摄入后可能对人体造成严重伤害甚至致命。

name: which is very poisonous and should never be added to drinking water.
trans: 这种物质具有很强的毒性，绝对不能被添加到饮用水中。

name: If no other safe water supply can be obtained,
trans: 如果无法获得其他安全的水源，

name: tap water that is too hot to touch can be left to cool and is generally safe to drink.
trans: 如果自来水太烫而无法直接饮用，可以将其放凉后再喝；通常情况下，这样的水是安全可饮用的。

name: Those planning a trip to remote areas, or intending to live in countries where drinking water is not readily available,
trans: 那些计划前往偏远地区旅行，或者打算生活在饮用水不易获得的国家的人，

name: should know about the various possible methods for making water safe.
trans: 应该了解各种使水变得安全的方法。

name: What every writer wants
trans: 每位作家都渴望拥有的东西

name: How do professional writers ignore what they were taught at school about writing?
trans: 专业作家是如何忽视他们在学校里学到的写作知识的呢？

name: I have known very few writers,
trans: 我认识的作家其实很少。

name: but those I have known and whom I respect, confess at once that they have little idea where they are going when they first set pen to paper.
trans: 但我认识且尊敬的人们都会坦承：当他们第一次拿起笔开始写作时，其实对自己要写什么、想要表达什么几乎一无所知（或者说，他们根本不知道自己该往哪个方向去写）。

name: They have a character, perhaps two;
trans: 他们有一个角色，也许还有两个角色。

name: they are in that condition of eager discomfort which passes for inspiration all admit radical changes of destination once the journey has begun;
trans: 他们都处于一种“急切不安”的状态；这种状态其实只是表面上的“灵感”罢了。所有人都承认：一旦旅程开始，目的地就会发生根本性的变化。

name: one, to my certain knowledge, spent nine months on a novel about Kashmir,
trans: 据我所知，有一个人花了九个月的时间来创作一部关于克什米尔的小说。

name: then reset the whole thing in the Scottish Highlands.
trans: 然后把整个系统重新设置到苏格兰高地。

name: I never heard of anyone making a 'skeleton', as we were taught at school.
trans: 我从未听说过有人会制作“骨架”（skeleton），这与我们在学校里学到的内容完全不同。

name: In the breaking and remaking, in the timing interweaving, beginning afresh,
trans: 在不断的破坏与重建中，在时间的交织与流转中，一切重新开始……

name: the writer comes to discern things in his material which were not consciously in his mind when he began.
trans: 作者在处理材料时，会发现一些自己开始写作时并未刻意考虑过的细节或元素。

name: This organic process, often leading to moments of extraordinary self-discovery, is of an indescribable fascination.
trans: 这个自然发生的过程常常会带来令人惊叹的自我发现时刻，其魅力实在难以用语言形容。

name: A blurred image appears; he adds a brushstroke and another and it is gone
trans: 一张模糊的图像出现了；他加了一笔、又加了一笔，然后那图像就消失了。

name: but something was there, and he will not rest till he has captured it.
trans: 但那里确实有什么东西；他不会罢休，直到抓住它为止。

name: Sometimes the yeast within a writer outlives a book he has written.
trans: 有时候，一个作家内心深处的“创造力”（或“灵感之源”）会比他写出的任何作品都更加持久、更加充满生命力。

name: I have heard of writers who read nothing but their own books;
trans: 我听说过有些作家，他们只读自己写的书。

name: like adolescents they stand before the mirror,
trans: 就像青少年一样，他们站在镜子前……

name: and still cannot fathom the exact outline of the vision before them.
trans: 他们仍然无法完全理解自己所面临的这个愿景的具体内容（或者说：他们仍然无法清晰地把握这个愿景的详细框架或核心要点）。

name: For the same reason, writers talk interminably about their own books,
trans: 出于同样的原因，作家们总是滔滔不绝地谈论自己的作品。

name: winkling out hidden meanings, super-imposing new ones,
trans: 揭示隐藏的含义，同时叠加新的意义……

name: begging response from those around them.
trans: 他们从周围的人那里寻求回应（或帮助）。

name: Of course a writer doing this is misunderstood: he might as well try to explain a crime or a love affair.
trans: 当然，这样的作家总是会被误解；他们其实就像是在试图解释一件犯罪行为或一段爱情故事一样——这两者都是极其复杂、难以用语言完全表达的事情。

name: He is also, incidentally, an unforgivable bore.
trans: 顺便说一下，他也是一个极其无趣、让人难以忍受的人。

name: This temptation to cover the distance between himself and the reader,
trans: 这种想要缩短自己与读者之间距离的冲动（或：这种想要拉近两者关系的欲望）……

name: to study his image in the sight of those who do not know him, can be his undoing: he has begun to write to please.
trans: 试图在那些不认识他的人眼中塑造自己的形象，反而可能成为他的致命弱点；他已经开始写作，只是为了取悦他人罢了。

name: A young English writer made the pertinent observation a year or two back
trans: 一年或两年前，一位年轻的英国作家提出了这一重要的观察意见。

name: that the talent goes into the first draft, and the art into the drafts that follow.
trans: 也就是说，才华体现在最初的草稿中，而艺术性则体现在后续的修改稿中。

name: For this reason also the writer, like any other artist,
trans: 正因如此，这位作家和其他艺术家一样，

name: has no resting place, no crowd or movement in which he may take comfort,
trans: 它无处可安息；无论在人群中还是喧闹的场面中，都无法找到片刻的慰藉。

name: no judgment from outside which can replace the judgment from within.
trans: 任何外部的评判都无法取代我们内心的判断。

name: A writer makes order out of the anarchy of his heart;
trans: 作家从自己内心中的混乱与无序中创造出秩序。

name: he submits himself to a more ruthless discipline than any critic dreamed of,
trans: 他自我约束的严格程度，超出了任何批评者所能想象的。

name: and when he flirts with fame, he is taking time off from living with himself,
trans: 当他追求名望时，他其实是在暂时停止与自己独处的时光。

name: from the search for what his world contains at its inmost point.
trans: 从对“他的世界在最深处的本质是什么”这一问题的探索中……

name: Waves
trans: 波浪

name: What false impression does an ocean wave convey to the observer?
trans: 海浪会给观察者留下什么样的错误印象呢？

name: Waves are the children of the struggle between ocean and atmosphere, the ongoing signatures of infinity.
trans: 海浪，是海洋与大气之间持续相互作用所产生的结果；它们象征着无穷无尽的自然力量与变化。

name: Rays from the sun excite and energize the atmosphere of the earth, awakening it to flow, to movement, to rhythm, to life.
trans: 太阳的光线激发并赋予地球大气层能量，使其开始流动、运动、产生节奏，并充满生机。

name: The wind then speaks the message of the sun to the sea
trans: 然后，风将太阳的信息传递给了大海。

name: and the sea transmits it on through waves--an ancient, exquisite powerful message.
trans: 海水通过海浪将这一信息传递出去——一条古老而精美的、充满力量的信息。

name: These ocean waves are among the earth's most complicated natural phenomena.
trans: 这些海浪是地球上最复杂的自然现象之一。

name: The basic features include a crest (the highest point of the wave),
trans: 基本特征包括波峰（即波浪的最高点）。

name: a trough (the lowest point), a height (the vertical distance from the trough to the crest),
trans: 一个低点（即最低位置），一个高度（即从低点到高点的垂直距离）。

name: a wave length (the horizontal distance between two wave crests),
trans: 波长（即两个波峰之间的水平距离）

name: and a period (which is the time it takes awave crest to travel one wave length).
trans: 以及一个点（这个点代表波峰传播一个波长的时间）。

name: Although an ocean wave gives the impression of a wall of water moving in your direction,
trans: 虽然海浪看起来像是一堵朝你方向涌来的水墙，

name: in actuality waves move through the water leaving the water about where it was.
trans: 实际上，波浪在水中传播时，只是将水从原来的位置“推开”到其他地方；波浪本身并不会离开水。

name: If the water was moving with the wave,
trans: 如果水是随着波浪一起运动的……

name: the ocean and everything on it would be racing in to the shore with obviously catastrophic results.
trans: 海洋以及海洋中的所有生物都会朝着海岸方向急速移动，这显然会导致灾难性的后果。

name: An ocean wave passing through deep water causes a particle on the surface to move in a roughly circular orbit,
trans: 当海浪穿过深水区域时，水面上的一个颗粒会沿着近似圆形的轨道运动。

name: drawing the particle first towards the advancing wave, then up into the wave,
trans: 首先将粒子吸引向前进的波浪，然后使其向上融入到波浪中。

name: then forward with it and then--as the wave leaves the particles behind--back to its starting point again.
trans: 然后继续这个过程；当那股“波浪”（或能量）离开那些粒子后，它又会重新回到它的起点。

name: From both maturity to death, a wave is subject to the same laws as any other 'living' thing.
trans: 从诞生到死亡，海浪与其他所有“生物”一样，都遵循着相同的自然规律。

name: For a time it assumes a miraculous individuality that, in the end, is reabsorbed into the great ocean of life.
trans: 在一段时间内，它展现出一种仿佛奇迹般的独特性；然而最终，这种独特性还是被重新融入了浩瀚的生命之海中。

name: The undulating waves of the open sea are generated by three natural causes:
trans: 开阔海域中那些起伏的波浪是由三种自然原因形成的：

name: wind, earth movements or tremors, and the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun.
trans: 风、地壳的运动（即地震），以及月球和太阳的引力作用。

name: Once waves have been generated,
trans: 一旦海浪被生成（或：波浪开始形成），

name: gravity is the force that drives them in a continual attempt to restore the ocean surface to a flat plain.
trans: 重力是一种力量，它促使海洋表面不断尝试恢复到平坦的状态。

name: Training elephants
trans: 训练大象

name: At what point does the training of a captive wild elephant begin?
trans: 圈养野生大象的训练是从什么时候开始的呢？

name: Two main techniques have been used for training elephants, which we may call respectively the tough and the gentle.
trans: 训练大象主要采用了两种方法，我们可以分别将它们称为“强硬型”方法与“温和型”方法。

name: The former method simply consists of setting an elephant to work and beating him until he does what is expected of him.
trans: 旧的方法很简单：就是让大象开始工作，然后不断地鞭打它，直到它按照要求去做为止。

name: Apart from any moral considerations this is a stupid method of training,
trans: 抛开任何道德方面的考虑不谈，这种训练方法实在愚蠢至极。

name: for it produces a resentful animal who at a later stage may well turn man-killer.
trans: 因为这会造就一只心怀怨恨的动物，而这种动物在未来很可能会变成杀人犯。

name: The gentle method requires more patience in the early stages,
trans: 这种温和的方法在初期需要更多的耐心。

name: but produce a cheerful good-tempered elephant who will give many years of loyal service.
trans: 不过，最终会诞生出一头性格开朗、脾气温和的大象，它将为我们提供多年忠诚的服务。

name: The first essential in elephant training is to assign to the animal a single mahout who will be entirely responsible for the job.
trans: 在大象训练中，首要的一点就是为每头大象指定一名专门的驯象师，这名驯象师将完全负责大象的训练工作。

name: Elephants like to have one master just as dogs do, and are capable of a considerable degree of personal affection.
trans: 大象和狗一样，也需要一个主人来照顾它们；它们也能够表现出相当程度的亲密情感（即对主人的喜爱或依赖）。

name: There are even stories of half-trained elephant calves who have refused to feed and pined to death
trans: 甚至还有这样的故事：那些只接受过部分训练的小象会拒绝进食，最终因饥饿而死亡。

name: when by some unavoidable circumstance they have been deprived of their own trainer.
trans: 当由于某些不可避免的情况，他们失去了自己的教练时……

name: Such extreme cases must probably be taken with a grain of salt,
trans: 对于这类极端案例，我们或许应该持保留态度（即不要完全相信它们的真实性）。

name: but they do underline the general principle that the relationship between elephant and mahout is the key to successful training.
trans: 但他们确实强调了这样一个基本原则：大象与驯象师之间的关系是成功训练大象的关键。

name: The most economical age to capture an elephant for training is between 15 and 20 years,
trans: 捕捉大象进行训练的最佳年龄是在15到20岁之间。

name: for it is then almost ready to undertake heavy work and can begin to earn its keep straight away.
trans: 因为那时它已经差不多准备好承担繁重的工作了，可以立即开始为自己创造价值（即开始赚钱或发挥其应有的作用）。

name: But animals of this age do not easily become subservient to man, and a very firm hand must be employed in the early stages.
trans: 但是这个年龄段的动物并不容易屈服于人类；在初期阶段，必须采取非常强硬的手段（或：必须使用强制性的方法）才能让它们服从人类的控制。

name: The captive elephant, still roped to a tree,
trans: 那头被囚禁的大象仍然被绳子拴在树上……

name: plunges and screams every time a man approaches, and for several days will probably refuse all food through anger and fear.
trans: 每当有男人靠近时，它就会惊慌失措、尖叫不已；出于愤怒和恐惧，它可能会连续几天拒绝进食。

name: Sometimes a tame elephant is tethered nearby to give the wild one confidence,
trans: 有时候，人们会把一头驯服的大象拴在附近，以此来让野生的大象感到安心（或有安全感）。

name: and in most cases the captive gradually quietens down and begins to accept its food.
trans: 在大多数情况下，被关押的动物会逐渐安静下来，并开始接受所提供的食物。

name: The next stage is to get the elephant to the training establishment,
trans: 下一个步骤是将大象送到训练机构去。

name: a ticklish business which is achieved with the aid of two tame elephants roped to the captive on either side.
trans: 这是一项需要小心处理的操作；具体方法是利用两头被驯服的大象，将它们用绳子拴在需要被移动的物体两侧，从而帮助完成这项工作。

name: When several elephants are being trained at one time,
trans: 当同时有多头大象正在接受训练时，

name: it is customary for the new arrival to be placed between the stalls of two captives whose training is already well advanced.
trans: 按照惯例，新来的成员会被安排到两名训练已经相当熟练的囚犯中间。

name: It is then left completely undisturbed with plenty of food and water
trans: 之后，它就被完全放任不管了，周围有充足的食物和水。

name: so that it can absorb the atmosphere of its new home and see that nothing particularly alarming is happening to its companions.
trans: 这样它就能适应新环境的气氛，并确认它的同伴们没有遇到任何特别令人担忧的问题。

name: When it is eating normally, its own training begins.
trans: 当它开始正常进食时，它的“自我训练”过程也就开始了。

name: The trainer stands in front of the elephant holding a long stick with a sharp metal point.
trans: 驯象师站在大象面前，手中拿着一根带有锋利金属尖端的长棍。

name: Two assistants, mounted on tame elephants, control the captive from either side,
trans: 两名助手骑在驯服的大象背上，从两侧分别控制着那个被囚禁的人。

name: while others rub their hands over his skin to the accompaniment of a monotonous and soothing chant.
trans: 而其他人则一边重复着单调而舒缓的咒语，一边用手轻轻抚摸他的皮肤。

name: This is supposed to induce pleasurable sensations in the elephant,
trans: 这应该是为了给大象带来愉悦的感觉。

name: and its effects are reinforced by the use of endearing epithets,
trans: 其效果通过使用那些亲切、可爱的称呼（或称谓）得到了进一步的强化。

name: such as 'ho! my son', or 'ho! my father', or 'my mother', according to the age and sex of the captive.
trans: 例如“嗬！我的儿子”或“嗬！我的父亲”，或者“我的母亲”——这些称呼会根据被俘者的年龄和性别来决定。

name: The elephant is not immediately susceptible to such blandishments, however, and usually lashes fiercely with its trunk in all directions.
trans: 然而，大象并不会立刻被这些花言巧语所打动；它通常会用鼻子猛烈地朝四面八方挥打。

name: These movements are controlled by the trainer with the metal-pointed stick,
trans: 这些动作是由训练者通过一根带有金属尖端的棍子来控制的。

name: and the trunk eventually becomes so sore that the elephant curls it up and seldom afterwards uses it for offensive purposes.
trans: 最终，大象的鼻子会变得非常疼痛；因此大象会将其蜷缩起来，之后也很少再使用它的鼻子来进行攻击性动作。

name: Recording an earthquake
trans: 记录地震数据

name: What does a pen have to do to record on paper the vibrations generated by an earthquake?
trans: 一支笔要如何才能在纸上记录下地震产生的震动呢？

name: An earthquake comes like a thief in the night, without warning.
trans: 地震就像夜间的小偷一样，毫无预兆地突然降临。

name: It was necessary, therefore, to invent instruments that neither slumbered nor slept.
trans: 因此，有必要发明那些既不会“沉睡”也不会“休息”的仪器（即那些能够持续运行、不会停止工作的设备）。

name: Some devices were quite simple.
trans: 有些设备的设计非常简单。

name: One, for instance, consisted of rods of various lengths and thicknesses which would stand up on end like ninepins.
trans: 例如，其中有一个装置由长度和厚度各不相同的杆子组成；这些杆子可以像九柱戏（ninepins）中的柱子一样竖立起来。

name: When a shock came, it shook the rigid table upon which these stood.
trans: 当那股冲击波传来时，它震动了那些物品所放置的坚硬桌子。

name: If it were gentle, only the more unstable rods fell.
trans: 如果这种作用力是温和的（即不剧烈的），那么只会是那些更加不稳定的杆子才会倒下。

name: If it were severe, they all fell.
trans: 如果情况严重的话，它们都会全部倒下。

name: Thus the rods, by falling, and by the direction in which they fell,
trans: 因此，这些杆子在下落的过程中，以及根据它们下落的方向……

name: recorded for the slumbering scientist the strength of a shock that was too weak to waken him,
trans: 为那位正在沉睡的科学家记录下了那次冲击的强度——不过那次冲击实在太微弱了，根本无法将他唤醒。

name: and the direction from which it came.
trans: 以及它来自的方向。

name: But instruments far more delicate than that were needed if any really serious advance was to be made.
trans: 但是，如果要取得真正重大的进展，就需要使用比那些仪器更加精密的设备。

name: The ideal to be aimed at was to devise an instrument that could record with a pen on paper,
trans: 我们的目标是设计一种能够用笔在纸上记录信息的工具。

name: the movements of the ground or of the table as the quake passed by.
trans: 地震发生时，地面或桌子的晃动情况。

name: While I write my pen moves, but the paper keeps still.
trans: 当我写字时，笔在动，但纸却静止不动。

name: With practice, no doubt, I could in time learn to write by holding the pen still while the paper moved.
trans: 通过练习，我相信我最终能够学会在纸张移动的同时保持笔静止不动来进行书写。

name: That sounds a silly suggestion,
trans: 那听起来真是个愚蠢的建议。

name: but that was precisely the idea adopted in some of the early instruments (seismometers) for recording earthquake waves.
trans: 但这正是某些早期地震仪在记录地震波时所采用的设计理念。

name: But when table, penholder and paper are all moving, how is it possible to write legibly?
trans: 但是当桌子、笔架和纸张都在移动时，怎么可能还能写出清晰可读的文字呢？

name: The key to a solution of that problem lay in an everyday observation.
trans: 解决那个问题的关键在于一个日常的观察结果。

name: Why does a person standing in a bus or train tend to fall when a sudden start is made?
trans: 为什么当公交车或火车突然启动时，站在上面的人容易摔倒呢？

name: It is because his feet move on, but his head stays still.
trans: 这是因为他的脚在不停地移动，但他的头部却保持静止不动。

name: A simple experiment will help us a little further.
trans: 一个简单的实验能帮助我们进一步理解这个原理。

name: Tie a heavy weight at the end of a long piece of string.
trans: 在一段较长的绳子末端系上一个重物。

name: With the hand held high in the air, hold the string so that the weight nearly touches the ground.
trans: 将绳子高高举过头顶，使重物几乎触碰到地面。

name: Now move the hand to and fro and around but not up and down.
trans: 然后让手在水平方向上前后移动，但不要上下移动。

name: It will be found that the weight moves but slightly or not at all.
trans: 你会发现，重物几乎不会移动，或者只会轻微移动。

name: Imagine a pen attached to the weight in such a way that its point rests upon a piece of paper on the floor.
trans: 想象一下，有一支笔被固定在重物上，其笔尖接触着地面上的一张纸。

name: Imagine an earthquake shock shaking the floor, the paper, you and your hand.
trans: 再想象一场地震，地震使地面、纸张以及你的手都在震动。

name: In the midst of all this movement, the weight and the pen would be still.
trans: 在所有这些震动中，重物和笔是静止的；

name: But as the paper moved from side to side under the pen point, its movement would be recorded in ink upon its surface.
trans: 但当纸张在笔尖下左右移动时，纸张的运动会通过墨水在纸上留下痕迹。

name: It was upon this principle that the first instruments were made, but the paper was wrapped round a drum which rotated slowly.
trans: 最早的测量仪器就是基于这个原理制造的——只不过当时的纸张是缠绕在一个缓慢旋转的鼓上的。

name: As long as all was still, the pen drew a straight line,
trans: 当一切保持静止时，笔会画出一条直线；

name: but while the drum was being shaken, the line that the pen was drawing wriggled from side to side.
trans: 而当鼓开始震动时，笔所画的线就会左右摇晃、变得弯曲不平。

name: The apparatus thus described, however,
trans: 然而，如此描述的这个装置……

name: records only the horizontal component of the wave movement, which is, in fact, much more complicated.
trans: 该设备仅记录了波浪运动的水平分量，而实际上波浪运动的过程要复杂得多。

name: If we could actually see the path described by a particle,
trans: 如果我们真的能够看到粒子所描绘的轨迹的话……

name: such as a sand grain in the rock,
trans: 就像岩石中的一粒沙子一样……

name: it would be more like that of a bluebottle buzzing round the room; it would be up and down, to and fro and from side to side.
trans: 它更像是一只蓝瓶子（一种昆虫）在房间里飞来飞去；它会上下移动，来回穿梭，从一边飞到另一边。

name: Instruments have been devised and can be so placed that all three elements can be recorded in different graphs.
trans: 已经设计出了相应的仪器，可以将这些仪器放置在与之相适应的位置，从而能够将这三个要素分别记录在不同的图表中。

name: When the instrument is situated at more than 700 miles from the earthquake centre,
trans: 当该仪器距离地震中心超过700英里时，

name: the graphic record shows three waves arriving one after the other at short intervals.
trans: 该图表显示有三波信号以较短的间隔依次传来。

name: The first records the arrival of longitudinal vibrations.
trans: 第一条记录显示了纵向振动的出现。

name: The second marks the arrival of transverse vibrations which travel more slowly and arrive several minutes after the first.
trans: 第二次震动标志着横向振动的开始；这些横向振动传播速度较慢，因此在第一次震动发生几分钟后才到达。

name: These two have travelled through the earth.
trans: 这两样东西已经穿越了整个地球。

name: It was from the study of these that so much was learnt about the interior of the earth.
trans: 正是通过对这些现象的研究，我们才对地球的内部结构有了如此多的了解。

name: The third, or main wave is the slowest and has travelled round the earth through the surface rocks.
trans: 第三波，也就是主波，是传播速度最慢的一波。它通过地表的岩石层在地球上进行了传播。

name: Are there strangers in space?
trans: 太空中有外星人吗？
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: What does the 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings in space depend on?
trans: 我们与太空中其他智慧生物进行交流的“独特且理性的方式”究竟取决于什么呢？
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: We must conclude from the work of those who have studied the origin of life,
trans: 我们必须从那些研究生命起源的科学家们的研究成果中得出结论。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: that given a planet only approximately like our own, life is almost certain to start.
trans: 只要有一颗行星的条件与我们的地球大致相似，生命几乎必然会诞生。

name: Of all the planets in our solar system, we are now pretty certain the Earth is the only one on which life can survive.
trans: 在我们太阳系中的所有行星中，我们现在可以相当确定：地球是唯一一个适合生命生存的星球。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: Mars is too dry and poor in oxygen, Venus far too hot, and so is Mercury,
trans: 火星太干燥且氧气含量极低；金星的温度过高；水星的情况也是如此。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: and the outer planets have temperatures near absolute zero and hydrogen-dominated atmospheres.
trans: 外行星的温度接近绝对零度，其大气层主要由氢气构成。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: But other suns, start as the astronomers call them, are bound to have planets like our own, and as is the number of stars in the universe is so vast,
trans: 但是其他恒星（正如天文学家所称的那样）很可能也拥有像我们地球这样的行星。而宇宙中的恒星数量如此庞大，因此……
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: this possibility becomes virtual certainty.
trans: 这种可能性几乎变成了必然的事实。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: There are one hundred thousand million starts in our own Milky Way alone,
trans: 仅在我们自己的银河系中，就存在着无数（100万亿）次恒星的诞生与消亡过程。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: and then there are three thousand million other milky ways or galaxies, in the universe.
trans: 此外，宇宙中还有另外三千亿个类似的星系（或“银河系”）。

name: so the number of stars that we know exist is now estimated at about 300 million million million.

name: Although perhaps only 1 percent of the life that has started somewhere will develop into highly complex and intelligent patterns,

name: so vast is the number of planets, that intelligent life is bound to be a natural part of the universe.
trans: 行星的数量如此之多，以至于智慧生命必定是宇宙中自然存在的一部分。
lesson: NCE4 · Are There Strangers in Space?

name: If then we are so certain that other intelligent life exists in the universe, why have we had no visitors from outer space yet?

name: First of all, they may have come to this planet of ours thousands or millions of years ago,
trans: 首先，他们可能早在几千甚至几百万年前就来到了我们的这个星球上。

name: and found our then prevailing primitive state completely uninteresting to their own advanced knowledge.
trans: 他们发现我们当时所处的原始状态，与他们自己所拥有的先进知识相比，完全毫无吸引力（或者说：他们认为我们的原始状态极其乏味、毫无价值）。

name: Professor Ronald Bracewell, a leading American radio astronomer,
trans: 罗纳德·布雷斯韦尔教授是美国著名的射电天文学家。

name: argued in Nature that such a superior civilization, on a visit to our own solar system,
trans: 《自然》杂志上有人提出这样的观点：如果一个高度先进的文明造访我们的太阳系，

name: may have left an automatic messenger behind to await the possible awakening of an advanced civilization.

name: although what impression any other civilization would thus get from us is best left unsaid.

name: though good enough to orbit men, have no chance of transporting us to the nearest other star,

name: Fortunately, there is a 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings,
